body_text: White-tailed eagles have returned to Exmoor after more than 200 years. Discover how this conservation project aims to restore one of the UK’s most iconic birds and strengthen biodiversity. White-Tailed Eagles Make a Historic Return to Exmoor A remarkable chapter in British wildlife conservation has begun as six white-tailed eagles have been released in Exmoor National Park for the first time in more than 200 years. The ambitious reintroduction project marks a major milestone in efforts to restore one of the UK’s largest birds of prey to landscapes where it once thrived. The release is part of a long-term conservation programme led by Forestry England and the Roy Dennis Wildlife Foundation. The initiative aims to rebuild the population of white-tailed eagles in southern England and encourage the species to establish a sustainable breeding presence in the South West. Known for their enormous wingspans of up to eight feet, white-tailed eagles are among the most impressive birds found in Britain. Sometimes described as “flying barn doors” because of their size and distinctive shape, these magnificent predators were once widespread across parts of England before persecution drove them to extinction in the region. Why White-Tailed Eagles Disappeared From Southern England White-tailed eagles were historically a natural part of Britain’s wildlife. However, centuries of hunting, habitat changes, and human persecution caused their numbers to decline dramatically. By the 18th century, the species had disappeared from southern England entirely. Their absence represented a significant loss for local ecosystems, as these birds play an important role as top predators and scavengers. The return of white-tailed eagles is not only about restoring a lost species. Conservation experts believe their presence can help improve biodiversity and restore natural ecological processes across coastal and rural areas. Exmoor Chosen as a New Home for Eagle Reintroduction Exmoor National Park, which stretches across parts of Devon and Somerset, was selected as a suitable location for the new releases after research showed that previously released birds were already exploring the area. Satellite tracking data from white-tailed eagles introduced on the Isle of Wight revealed that some birds frequently travelled to Exmoor. The region offers many of the features these large predators need, including coastal habitats, rivers, open landscapes, and access to food sources such as fish and other wildlife. The area also has historical significance, as white-tailed eagles would have naturally bred across parts of south-west England before disappearing. Before the release took place, conservation organisations carried out feasibility studies, public consultations, and environmental assessments. Local groups and community representatives have also been involved through a project steering group designed to support the long-term success of the programme. A Continuing Conservation Success Story The Exmoor release builds on the progress of a wider white-tailed eagle restoration project that began with releases on the Isle of Wight in 2019. Since then, 45 young white-tailed eagles have been released as part of the southern England reintroduction effort. The programme achieved a major breakthrough in 2023 when the first wild white-tailed eagle chick was born in southern England for more than 240 years. This successful breeding event demonstrated that released birds could adapt, survive, and eventually contribute to the recovery of the species. Conservationists expect the newly released Exmoor birds to travel widely while they mature. White-tailed eagles usually begin breeding when they are around four to five years old, meaning the full impact of the project will develop over time. More Eagles Planned for Exmoor The conservation team has announced plans to release up to 20 additional young white-tailed eagles from the Exmoor site over the next three years. Releases will also continue from the Isle of Wight as part of the broader effort to rebuild the species’ population. Experts will closely monitor the birds using tracking technology to understand their movements, survival rates, and future breeding behaviour. Zoe Smith from the Roy Dennis Wildlife Foundation said the return of white-tailed eagles to Exmoor represents a special moment after centuries of absence. The team will continue following the birds’ progress as they explore the region and eventually establish themselves within the landscape. Boost for Biodiversity Across the UK The return of white-tailed eagles is expected to bring wider environmental benefits. As a key species within ecosystems, these birds help maintain natural balance by influencing populations of other animals and contributing to nutrient recycling. Ali Hawkins, senior ecologist with Exmoor National Park Authority, described the release as an exciting moment for the national park and a significant boost for biodiversity. The project reflects growing efforts across the UK to restore native species that have disappeared due to historical pressures. Similar conservation programmes have focused on bringing back endangered or extinct-in-the-wild species, while improving habitats for many other plants and animals. Government Support for Wildlife Recovery The latest eagle release has also received support from the UK Government. Environment Secretary Angela Eagle welcomed the return of the birds, highlighting it as part of wider commitments to protect nature and reverse wildlife declines. The Government has also pointed to funding initiatives aimed at supporting threatened species recovery and improving biodiversity across the country. The return of white-tailed eagles demonstrates how carefully managed conservation projects can help repair damage caused by centuries of environmental change. While the birds still face challenges, including habitat pressures and the need for successful breeding, their return offers hope for the future of British wildlife. What the Return of White-Tailed Eagles Means for Exmoor For local communities, visitors, and wildlife enthusiasts, the arrival of white-tailed eagles marks an exciting new era for Exmoor. These birds are expected to become an important part of the region’s natural identity and could attract greater interest in conservation and wildlife tourism. The project is also a reminder that species once lost from landscapes can sometimes return through scientific research, public support, and long-term commitment. After more than two centuries away, white-tailed eagles are once again flying above Exmoor. Their journey back represents not only the recovery of a remarkable bird but also a wider effort to restore the connection between Britain’s landscapes and the wildlife that once called them home. Source The Independent, August 04 2026. Disclaimer This article is a rewritten and independently produced summary created for informational purposes. Details have been adapted from publicly available reporting and may change as the conservation project develops.

title: Healthcare Cybersecurity Statistics for 2026: Breach Costs, Ransomware, and Patient Safety Impact
summary: Healthcare entered 2026 still absorbing the largest cyberattack in the history of US medicine.
body_text: Healthcare entered 2026 still absorbing the largest cyberattack in the history of US medicine. As of July 31, 2025, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services confirmed that the Change Healthcare ransomware attack impacted approximately 192.7 million individuals, nearly two thirds of the US population. Across the wider sector, healthcare data breaches cost an average of $7.42 million per incident in 2025, the highest of any industry for the 14th consecutive year, according to the IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025 . And Verizon's 2025 Data Breach Investigations Report logged 1,710 healthcare incidents with 1,542 confirmed disclosures, with system intrusion and ransomware now the top breach pattern in the sector. These are the healthcare cybersecurity statistics IT, security, and compliance leaders need to know going into 2026. Key healthcare cybersecurity statistics at a glance 192.7 million individuals were affected by the Change Healthcare ransomware attack, per the HHS Office for Civil Rights . It is the largest healthcare breach ever reported. $7.42 million was the average cost of a healthcare data breach in 2025, the highest of any industry studied, per the IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025 . Healthcare has led every industry for 14 straight years. 279 days was the average time to identify and contain a healthcare breach in 2025, five weeks longer than the global average, per IBM . 697 large healthcare data breaches were reported to the HHS OCR breach portal in 2025, exposing the protected health information of at least 61.5 million individuals. 1,710 healthcare security incidents and 1,542 confirmed data disclosures were tracked by the Verizon 2025 DBIR , with system intrusion overtaking miscellaneous errors as the top pattern. 33% of healthcare ransomware incidents in 2025 began with exploited vulnerabilities, the most common technical root cause for the first time in three years, per Sophos State of Ransomware in Healthcare 2025 . 58% of healthcare providers hit by ransomware recovered within a week in 2025, more than double the 21% reported in 2024, per Sophos . 460 ransomware incidents in the healthcare and public health sector were reported to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center in 2024, the highest of any critical infrastructure subsector. Nearly 1 in 4 healthcare delivery organizations surveyed reported an increase in patient mortality rates after a ransomware attack, per the Ponemon Institute . $3.09 billion was the total reported direct cost of the Change Healthcare cyberattack to UnitedHealth Group through the third quarter of 2024, per UnitedHealth Group's SEC filing . ‍ Breach volume and PHI exposure: what the HHS portal shows The HHS Office for Civil Rights publishes every healthcare breach of 500 or more individuals on its public breach portal . The 2025 ledger lists 697 large incidents, a 6% reduction from 742 in 2024, but with extraordinary concentration of harm. Even with the lower count, at least 61.5 million individuals had their protected health information exposed or impermissibly disclosed in 2025. Including the upward revision of the Change Healthcare total to 192.7 million in July 2025, the headline figures for the sector remain historic. The portal breaks 2025 reports down by entity type: 523 incidents at healthcare providers, 56 at health plans, two at clearinghouses, and 128 at business associates of HIPAA covered entities. The location of breached PHI is now dominated by network servers (61.5% of incidents) and email accounts (24.9%), per HHS data . That mix is a clear signal that hospitals are no longer losing PHI to laptops left in cars; the modern healthcare breach is a network compromise. The cost of a healthcare breach in 2025 Healthcare's average breach cost dropped from $9.77 million in 2024 to $7.42 million in 2025, per the IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025 . Even with the year over year improvement, healthcare remained the most expensive industry studied for the 14th straight year. The same IBM research found healthcare also has the longest breach lifecycle of any industry at 279 days from intrusion to containment, more than five weeks above the global average of 241 days. Detection and containment delays are the single biggest driver of healthcare breach costs because every additional day of attacker dwell time multiplies the volume of PHI at risk and the operational hit to patient care. The economics show up clearly at the enterprise level. UnitedHealth Group reported in its Q3 2024 8-K filing that direct response costs from the Change Healthcare attack reached $3.09 billion through the first nine months of 2024, with full year impact projected as high as $2.45 billion in direct costs alone before factoring in lost revenue and business disruption. The company also provided more than $9 billion in advance funding and interest free loans to help downstream providers stay solvent while claims and pharmacy systems were offline. Ransomware in hospitals: who is paying, who is recovering Ransomware economics in healthcare changed sharply in 2025. The Sophos State of Ransomware in Healthcare 2025 report, based on a survey of 292 healthcare IT and security leaders, found median ransom demands against healthcare providers fell 91% year over year to $343,000, down from $4 million in 2024. Median ransom payments dropped from $1.47 million to just $150,000. The share of hospitals paying any ransom slipped to 36% in 2025, down from 61% in 2022. Recovery has accelerated, too. 58% of healthcare providers hit by ransomware in 2025 were back online within a week, more than double the 21% who said the same in 2024, per Sophos . Two attacker tactics shifted at the same time. Encryption based attacks fell to 34% of incidents (from 74% in 2024), while extortion only attacks (data theft without encryption) tripled to 12% of cases. The headline takeaway: attackers are stealing more, encrypting less, and asking for less because providers have gotten better at refusing to pay. Root causes tell the operational story. For the first time in three years, exploited vulnerabilities (33% of attacks) edged out compromised credentials as the leading technical root cause in healthcare, per Sophos . The most common organizational factor was a lack of in house cybersecurity capacity, cited by 42% of victim organizations. Sophos X-Ops identified 88 distinct ransomware groups actively targeting healthcare in 2025. What the Verizon DBIR says about healthcare attack patterns The Verizon 2025 Data Breach Investigations Report analyzed 1,710 healthcare security incidents and 1,542 confirmed data disclosures during the report period. System intrusion, which includes ransomware and extortion, overtook miscellaneous errors as the top pattern in healthcare, mirroring the broader industry shift. External actors caused 67% of healthcare breaches, insiders 30%, partners 4%, and 1% involved multiple parties. 90% of attacks on healthcare were financially motivated. The most striking new datapoint from Verizon is an espionage motive: 16% of healthcare breaches in 2024 carried an espionage element, up from just 1% the year prior. That sixteen fold increase suggests a new class of actor (likely nation state aligned) is now actively pursuing US medical research, clinical trial data, and patient records. Verizon also reported that healthcare breaches involving a business associate or vendor doubled in one year, jumping from 15% to 30% of all incidents. Patient safety: when cyberattacks become clinical events Healthcare is the only industry where a cyberattack can directly lengthen a hospital stay or end a life. Research published by the Ponemon Institute (in partnership with Proofpoint) found that more than 20% of healthcare organizations hit by the four most common attack types (cloud compromise, ransomware, supply chain attacks, and business email compromise) experienced increased patient mortality rates after the incident. Nearly 1 in 4 providers reported the same outcome specifically following a ransomware attack. Operational disruption is even more common. Per the same Ponemon research, ransomware caused procedure or test delays at 64% of victim organizations, longer patient stays at 59%, increased patient transfers or facility diversions at 65%, and complications from medical procedures at 36%. The Ascension Health ransomware attack in May 2024 (which exposed PHI for 5.6 million patients) forced ambulance diversions and paused elective care across the system. Ascension reported a $1.1 billion net loss for fiscal 2024, citing the cyberattack as a material factor. Third party and business associate risk Healthcare's biggest 2025 cyber story (the Change Healthcare breach) was a business associate event. So is the fastest growing risk vector in the sector. According to Verizon , the share of healthcare breaches involving a business associate doubled in one year, from 15% to 30%. The HHS breach portal lists 128 business associate breaches in 2025, accounting for a disproportionate share of total records exposed because vendors aggregate data from many covered entities. The HHS Office for Civil Rights has been explicit that covered entities cannot outsource HIPAA liability. Under 45 CFR 164.404, covered entities remain responsible for ensuring affected individual notifications occur after a business associate breach, even when the business associate (such as UnitedHealth Group in the Change Healthcare case) volunteers to handle notification. That regulatory baseline means risk analysis of every business associate and a current business associate agreement on file are no longer optional controls. Emerging trends and what is new in 2026 Three trends define healthcare cybersecurity heading into 2026. Espionage now sits beside extortion. The Verizon 2025 DBIR jump from 1% to 16% espionage motive in healthcare breaches is the most consequential year over year shift in the report. Hospitals and biotech research organizations now face actors interested in intellectual property and patient cohort data, not just ransom payments. These actors are harder to detect than ransomware crews because they do not announce themselves. Critical infrastructure status is a target, not a shield. The FBI IC3 2024 Annual Report recorded 460 ransomware incidents in the healthcare and public health sector, the highest of any critical infrastructure subsector. The Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2025 framed why: ransomware actors focus on hospitals because the consequences of downtime (potential patient harm) leave administrators with fewer options than CEOs in other sectors. The same Microsoft report found that 52% of all financially motivated cyberattacks with a known motive are now driven by extortion and ransomware. Detection still lags by months, not days. The IBM 279 day healthcare breach lifecycle is the longest of any industry, and the gap between healthcare and the global average (241 days) is widening. That detection lag is the cost driver every CISO can act on in 2026. Endpoint visibility, identity monitoring, and vulnerability remediation have a measurable impact on dwell time, and dwell time is what turns a $1 million incident into a $10 million one. For broader context on the trends above, see our ransomware statistics and data breach statistics roundups. title: How to Write Off Business Expenses: A Practical Guide for Small Business Owners
summary: How to write off business expenses under IRS §162 ordinary and necessary rule, deductible categories, documentation requirements, and where to record each type of deduction.
body_text: Writing off a business expense means deducting it from your business's taxable income. Under Internal Revenue Code Section 162 , an expense is deductible if it is both "ordinary" common and accepted in your trade and "necessary" helpful and appropriate to business. That is entire legal test, and it covers almost every real business expense you incur. The practical work is knowing which specific categories IRS allows, how each is documented, what percentage is deductible, and where each shows up on tax return. What "writing off" actually means Three phrases get used interchangeably but mean different things: Tax deduction reduces taxable income. Every dollar deducted saves you tax at your marginal rate. A $1,000 deduction at a 24% marginal rate saves $240. Tax credit reduces tax dollar-for-dollar. A $1,000 credit saves $1,000. Much rarer than deductions. Write-off informal term usually meaning "deduction," but sometimes used to describe writing off a bad debt (uncollectible receivable) or an impaired asset (obsolete inventory). When most business owners say "write it off," they mean take a deduction. The rest of this guide covers deductions specifically. The IRS Section 162 test Every business expense you deduct has to pass same two-part test in IRS Publication 535 : Ordinary common and accepted in your trade or business Necessary helpful and appropriate for business "Necessary" does not mean indispensable. A conference registration is necessary if it advances your business, even if you could theoretically run business without going. Expenses that meet test are deductible in year paid (cash-basis) or incurred (accrual-basis). Expenses that create a long-term asset laptops, vehicles, buildings, equipment with useful lives over 1 year are generally capitalized rather than expensed. See our fixed asset accounting guide for how to handle those. Common categories of deductible business expenses Almost every deductible expense falls into one of these categories. Track them by category in your bookkeeping that maps directly to tax return line items. Advertising and marketing. Fully deductible. Includes website costs, ads, printed materials, sponsorships, and business branding. 100% deductible. Bank and merchant processing fees. Fully deductible. Monthly bank fees, credit card processor fees (Stripe, Square, PayPal), wire fees, ACH fees. 100% deductible. Business insurance. Fully deductible. General liability, professional liability, workers' comp, cyber, product liability. Health insurance for self-employed owners is separately deductible on personal return (not Schedule C). Business meals. 50% deductible in most cases. 100% deductible for company events open to all employees (holiday parties) and for meals sold to customers. Entertainment is 0% deductible after TCJA. Contract labor / independent contractors. Fully deductible. Amounts paid to freelancers, agencies, consultants. Requires 1099-NEC for any contractor paid $600 or more in a year. Depreciation. Deduction for long-lived assets spread over their useful life. Section 179 and bonus depreciation allow first-year expensing of many items. Employee benefits. Health insurance, retirement plan contributions, group life insurance, education assistance. Employer-side portion is deductible. Home office (self-employed only). Deductible on Form 8829 if you use a portion of your home regularly and exclusively for business. Simplified method: $5/sq ft, up to 300 sq ft = $1,500 max. Legal and professional fees. Fully deductible. Attorney fees for business matters, accountant fees (including tax prep for business return), consulting fees. Office rent. Fully deductible. Includes coworking memberships. Office supplies and small equipment. Fully deductible if under de minimis safe harbor ($2,500 per item invoice, or $5,000 with applicable financial statements). Larger items get capitalized and depreciated. Software subscriptions. Fully deductible. Includes SaaS, project management tools, accounting software, communication tools. Startup costs. Up to $5,000 deductible in year 1 (phases out if total startup costs exceed $50,000); remainder amortized over 15 years under Section 195. Supplies used in operations. Fully deductible. Materials consumed in ordinary course. Telephone and internet. Deductible for business use portion. Separate business lines are 100% deductible; shared home lines are prorated. Travel. Fully deductible for business portion. Airfare, lodging, ground transportation, business meals during travel (50% rule applies). Utilities. Fully deductible for business locations. Home-office utilities are prorated (part of Form 8829 calculation). Vehicle expenses. Either standard mileage rate ( see 2026 rates ) or actual expenses. The choice in year 1 of ownership determines future flexibility. Documentation requirements The IRS's audit standard for deductions is contemporaneous documentation. That means record was made at or near time of expense, not reconstructed later from memory or credit card statements. What you need to keep, per deduction category: Receipts for any expense over $75 (IRS's small-expense threshold for most cases). Below $75, credit card statement usually suffices, but keeping receipt anyway is safer. Mileage log date, business purpose, starting/ending location, miles. Required contemporaneous, not reconstructed. Home office measurements, photos, description of exclusive use. Utilities and rent bills for year. Business meals receipt, plus business purpose and attendees (who and why). "Lunch with client X to discuss project Y" is sufficient documentation. Travel receipts for airfare, lodging, ground transport. Notes on business purpose per day of trip. 1099 contractor payments signed Form W-9 from contractor, 1099-NEC filed by January 31 following year. Depreciation invoice, in-service date, useful life, method chosen. Retention: 7 years is safe rule for most business records. Employment tax records: 4 years minimum. Property records: while owned + 4 years after disposition. See our guide on how long to keep business tax records for full retention schedule. What is NOT deductible Common non-deductible expenses that trip up new business owners: Personal expenses never deductible even if paid from business account Commuting driving from home to your regular workplace is not deductible (see mileage rate guide for deductible-mile rules) Political contributions and lobbying non-deductible under IRC §162(e) Fines and penalties parking tickets, IRS penalties, regulatory fines all non-deductible Entertainment 0% deductible after TCJA (was 50% before 2018) Country club and gym memberships non-deductible even if used for business networking Life insurance premiums on owner/employees where business is beneficiary non-deductible Where to record deductions by entity type Which tax form and line depends on your business structure: Sole proprietor / single-member LLC (default) Schedule C, Form 1040 Multi-member LLC (partnership) Form 1065, expenses flow through K-1 S-corp Form 1120-S, expenses flow through K-1 C-corp Form 1120, expenses reduce corporate taxable income Self-employed retirement plan contributions Adjustments to Income on Form 1040, not Schedule C Health insurance premiums (self-employed) Above-the-line deduction on Form 1040 Schedule 1 For most single-owner businesses, bookkeeping category maps directly to a Schedule C line . Getting categorization right during year rather than reconstructing at tax time saves hours of April cleanup and reduces audit risk. Conclusion Every deductible expense passes same test: ordinary and necessary for trade or business. Categorize consistently during year, keep documentation contemporaneous, and know four or five special rules (50% meals, home office simplified vs actual, mileage year-1 choice, startup cost phase-out) that trip up most first-time filers. FAQ Can I write off my car for business? Yes, if you use it for business. Choose standard mileage rate (multiplier per mile) or actual expenses (business-use percentage of every actual cost). The year-1 choice affects your ability to switch later. Only business miles count commuting from home to a regular workplace is not deductible. Can I write off my phone bill? Yes, for business-use portion. A dedicated business line is 100% deductible. A shared personal/business phone is deductible for business percentage track approximate business use to justify deduction. Can I write off business meals? Generally 50% deductible. Meals must be with a business purpose (client, prospect, employee travel) and reasonable. 100% deductible for company events open to all employees and for meals sold to customers. Entertainment is 0% deductible. How much of a home office can I deduct? Under simplified method: $5/square foot, up to 300 sq ft = $1,500 maximum. Under regular method (Form 8829): actual home expenses × business-use percentage. Regular method usually produces a larger deduction if your home has meaningful utilities and mortgage interest. Are startup costs deductible? Yes, up to $5,000 in year 1 under IRC §195 (phased out if total startup costs exceed $50,000). Remainder amortized over 15 years. This includes market research, employee training before opening, professional fees for incorporation. What business expenses can I NOT write off? Personal expenses, commuting, political contributions, fines and penalties, entertainment (post-TCJA), country club dues, life insurance premiums where business is beneficiary. Also: expenses reimbursed by insurance (you got money back). Do I need receipts for every expense? For expenses over $75, keep receipt. Under $75, credit card statements and bank records usually suffice but keeping receipts anyway costs nothing and eliminates audit friction. Business meals, travel, and vehicle expenses always need documentation regardless of amount. Where do I record business expenses on my tax return? Sole proprietors and single-member LLCs: Schedule C. Partnerships and multi-member LLCs: Form 1065. S-corps: Form 1120-S. C-corps: Form 1120. Each form has specific line items that map to bookkeeping categories above.

body_text: Red Cat Reports Q2 2026 Revenue Growth of 527% Y/Y; Q2 Gross Margins Increase 39% vs Q2 2025; Gross Margins Increased 27% Sequentially from Q1 2026 August 06, 2026 4:05pm EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio 10-Q HTML PDF XBRL Zip SALT LAKE CITY, Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Red Cat Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: RCAT) ("Red Cat" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based provider of advanced all-domain drone and robotic solutions for defense and national security, reports its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Total revenue: $20.2 million, an increase of 527% compared to Q2 2025. Gross profit: $3.3 million, an increase of $2.9 million from Q2 2025. Gross margin: 16.1%, representing a year-over-year improvement of 39% from Q2 2025, and a sequential improvement of 27% from Q1 2026. Business Highlights Red Cat’s Teal Drones Advances to Gauntlet II of Drone Dominance Program, positioning Teal Drones among a select group of finalists competing in the next phase of a potentially significant procurement opportunity focused on rapidly fielding low-cost, attributable drone systems for U.S. military operations. Completed the acquisition of Quaze Technologies, adding wireless power transfer technology that addresses one of the most significant barriers to persistent autonomy. Quaze's charging architecture enables autonomous recharging and supports longer-duration operations across drones, robotic systems and uncrewed maritime platforms. Introduced Hellcat™, a globally configurable small UAS platform built on the proven Black Widow architecture, expanding Red Cat's international addressable market with a platform designed to support allied defense customers worldwide. Expanded Red Cat's autonomy capabilities through joint product development and demonstrations where Red Cat and Apium presented a multi-vendor, find, fix, finish solution under a single command and control, including ISR provided by Black Widow, with kinetic finish by Fang 7 orchestrated by Apium's Paradigm autonomy. Secured contract between Blue Ops and U.S. Navy to lease its Variant 7 and participate in testing, integration, and electronic warehouse under the U.S. Navy's Office of Naval Research. Scaled Blue Ops into a leading maritime operations platform by driving the U.S.-built Variant 7 uncrewed surface vessel to full-rate production and successfully launched and validated the latest variant of our 5 meter USV, advancing our maritime autonomy roadmap expanding autonomous capabilities across air, land and sea platforms. Apium and Blue Ops have been selected to participate in the U.S. Office of Naval Research Global's mACE3 and mACE4 operational experimentation events at MCAS Cherry Point, North Carolina, highlighting continued engagement with the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps on advanced autonomous maritime capabilities. Secured new orders from the U.S. Air Force Security Forces for Black Widow™ drones, train-the-trainer support, batteries, and mission critical spares. "Our second quarter results reflect the continued execution of a strategy that is transforming Red Cat into a leading all-domain autonomy platform for defense and national security," said Jeff Thompson, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Red Cat. "Revenue increased more than fivefold year-over-year as we scaled deliveries, expanded production capacity and continued to invest in technologies that enhance our competitive position across air, land and maritime operations. We also expanded gross margins 39% year-over-year and 27% sequentially, demonstrating the benefits of scale, production efficiencies and a more diversified product portfolio. During the quarter, we advanced to Gauntlet II of the Drone Dominance program, ramped Blue Ops into full-rate production, completed the acquisition of Quaze Technologies and continued expanding our autonomy, power and robotic capabilities through strategic investments. Together, these initiatives strengthen our ability to deliver integrated solutions that help customers deploy, sustain and scale autonomous operations in increasingly complex environments. With more than $325 million of cash on the balance sheet, expanding manufacturing capacity and a growing Family of Systems spanning air, land and sea, we believe Red Cat is uniquely positioned to capitalize on the accelerating adoption of unmanned and autonomous systems. We remain focused on executing against the significant opportunities in front of us and progressing toward our revenue outlook." Balance Sheet Cash at June 30, 2026 totaled $325.6 million, compared to $167.9 million at December 31, 2025. Inventory and prepaid inventory at June 30, 2026 totaled $84.8 million, compared to $30.4 million at December 31, 2025. Target Revenue Red Cat is reaffirming its full year target revenue in the range of $150 million and $180 million. title: Grab Bar Installation for Seniors: Placement & Cost
summary: Learn where to install grab bars for seniors, the correct height, and why professional installation matters. GoGo arranges vetted local help by phone.
body_text: Grab Bar Installation for Seniors: Where to Place Them and How to Get It Done Right A grab bar looks like a simple piece of hardware, but for an older adult, it can be the difference between a safe day and a trip to the emergency room. Falls send millions of seniors to the hospital every year, and the bathroom is one of the most common places they happen. Wet tile, a slick tub edge, and the act of lowering or raising yourself off a toilet all create moments where a sturdy handhold matters. Getting grab bars installed correctly is one of the most affordable and effective changes you can make to help a senior stay safe at home. This guide covers where grab bars belong, how high they should sit, why professional installation matters, and how to arrange it without a lot of hassle. Why Grab Bars Matter for Seniors Balance changes with age. So do grip strength, eyesight, and reaction time. A younger person who slips can usually catch themselves. An older adult often cannot, and a single fall can lead to a broken hip, a head injury, or a long recovery that chips away at independence. Grab bars give the body a fixed, reliable point to hold. They help with the small transitions that happen dozens of times a day, like stepping into the shower, standing up from the toilet, or steadying yourself while you dry off. For someone recovering from surgery or living with arthritis, that support removes a real source of daily anxiety. Where to Install Grab Bars The bathroom is the priority, and three spots do the most good. Inside the shower or tub, a horizontal or angled bar on the wall gives support while stepping over the edge and while standing. Next to the toilet, a bar mounted on the side wall or a swing-away model helps with sitting down and standing up, which is where a lot of falls happen. By the tub entry, a bar positioned where someone steps in and out reduces the risk during the most slippery moment of the routine. Bathrooms are not the only place bars help. Hallways, stairwells, and entryways with a step or two are all worth considering, especially if the senior uses a walker or cane. Getting the Heights & Placement Right Placement is not guesswork. The generally accepted guidance, drawn from ADA standards, puts horizontal grab bars between 33 and 36 inches above the floor. Bars should be long enough to grip comfortably, usually 24 to 36 inches, and mounted so the hand has room to wrap around fully. Angle matters too. A bar set at a slight diagonal near a tub can be easier to grip while moving up or down than a strictly horizontal one. The right choice depends on the person's height, which side is stronger, and how they actually move through the space. A good installer looks at the room and the person, not just the wall. Choosing the Right Grab Bar Not all grab bars are the same, and the right one depends on the person and the spot. Look for a bar rated to hold a real load, ideally 250 pounds or more, since the whole point is that it holds when someone leans hard on it. A textured or knurled surface gives a better grip for wet or weak hands than a smooth chrome finish. Finish matters for visibility too, and a bar in a color that contrasts with the wall is easier for someone with low vision to find. If cost is a concern, a professional can help you focus on the highest-value spots first rather than doing everything at once. Why Professional Installation Matters Here is the part people underestimate. A grab bar is only as strong as what it is anchored to. Screwed into drywall alone, a bar can pull loose the moment real weight lands on it, and a bar that fails during a fall is worse than no bar at all, because the person was trusting it. Proper installation means mounting into wall studs or using heavy-duty blocking and anchors rated for the load. A professional knows how to find the studs, choose the right hardware for tile or fiberglass, and seal the mounting points so water does not get behind the wall. If your bathroom layout does not line up with the studs, an experienced installer has ways to solve that, from mounting plates to backing boards. That problem-solving is hard to replicate on your own. Grab Bar Installation Costs Cost depends on how many bars you need, the wall material, and your area. A single bar in a straightforward spot is an inexpensive job. Tile walls, multiple bars, or tricky layouts push the price up because they take more time and skill. The honest answer is that you want an estimate before the work starts, so there are no surprises. Grab bars also pair naturally with other safety upgrades. If you are already improving the bathroom, it can make sense to look at plumbing fixtures like a handheld showerhead or brighter lighting and electrical work to reduce shadows. Handling several small jobs in one visit is usually more efficient than booking them separately. How to arrange grab bar installation the easy way For many seniors and their families, the hardest part is not deciding to install grab bars. It is finding someone trustworthy to do it, especially when a parent lives in another city. GoGoGrandparent takes that work off your plate. You call, tell a live operator what you need, and they match you with a vetted, background-checked local pro. There is no app to download and no account to set up. If you are arranging it for a parent, you can give their address from anywhere and stay in the loop while the work gets done. Grab bar installation is part of GoGo's full handyman services for seniors , which sit within a wider set of home services built around helping older adults stay independent. Families who want ongoing support can also look at regular wellness checks or a membership plan that makes future requests simple. A grab bar is a small thing. The safety and confidence it gives back is not. If there is an older adult in your life who could use one, it is worth handling sooner rather than after a fall makes the case for you.

title: Form 1040-X: How to Amend Your Tax Return (Deadlines, E-File, Refund Tracking)
summary: Form 1040-X explained amended US tax return you file to correct errors on a prior 1040. Three-year statute of limitations, when to e-file vs paper, tracking refunds via Where's My Amended Return, and situations that don't require amending.
body_text: Form 1040-X is Amended US Individual Income Tax Return form you file when you need to correct an error on a previously filed Form 1040. Missed deduction? Forgot a W-2? Discovered a K-1 that arrived after you filed? Wrong filing status? Amend with a 1040-X. The IRS gives you three years from original filing date (or two years from when tax was paid, whichever is later) to submit changes and claim any refund. This guide walks through when to amend, three-year statute of limitations, how to e-file 1040-X (available since 2020), what to include, how long processing takes, and how to track your amended refund via Where's My Amended Return. What Form 1040-X does Per IRS Form 1040-X page , Form 1040-X is used to correct any information on a previously filed Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR. Common reasons to amend: Missed income a late 1099, missed W-2, or K-1 that arrived after filing Missed deduction or credit realized you qualified for something (e.g., Earned Income Credit, education credit, home office) Filing status change got married and want to change from Single to MFJ, or realized you qualify for Head of Household Wrong dependents added or removed a dependent Miscalculated tax math errors, wrong bracket applied, wrong withholding entered Wrong income allocation moved states mid-year and misallocated to state returns Form 1040-X does NOT amend state returns each state has its own amended-return process. Amend federal first, then state. The three-year statute of limitations You have LATER of: 3 years from original filing date, OR 2 years from date you paid tax ...to file a 1040-X and claim a refund. After that, you can amend to REPORT change (still required for accuracy), but you cannot receive a refund of overpaid tax. Example: Original 2021 return filed on April 15, 2022 Refund claim deadline: April 15, 2025 (3 years from filing) Extended returns: If you extended your filing deadline (Form 4868), 3-year clock starts on actual filing date (or October 15, whichever is earlier). Balances owed: If you're amending to REPORT additional tax owed, you should file as soon as possible penalties and interest continue to accrue until you pay. E-filing Form 1040-X (available for 2019+) Since 2020, IRS accepts electronic Form 1040-X for tax years 2019 and later. E-filing: Processes in ~3 weeks vs. up to 16+ weeks for paper Requires original return to have been e-filed (paper-filed originals must amend by paper) Available through most tax software (TurboTax, H&R Block, Drake, Lacerte, ProConnect, TaxAct) Direct deposit available for refunds on e-filed 1040-X since 2023 Paper filing (required if): Original return was paper-filed Amending tax year 2018 or earlier Amending an amended return (you can amend a 1040-X, but by paper only) Certain state issues that require attached documentation Mail paper 1040-X to IRS service center for your state. Include all corrected schedules and supporting documents. Section-by-section: what Form 1040-X looks like Form 1040-X has three columns and space for you to explain change: Column A Original amount. What you originally reported on Form 1040. Get this from your originally filed return (not what you should have reported). Column B Net change. The increase or decrease in each line as a result of amendment. Column C Correct amount. What line SHOULD show after amendment. (Column A + Column B = Column C.) Part III Explanation of Changes. Free-text field where you explain what changed and why. Be specific: "Missed 1099-NEC from XYZ Corp $8,500 added to Schedule C Line 1 gross receipts. Recalculated Line 31 net profit and Schedule SE. Additional tax owed: $1,320." Attach corrected schedules. Any schedule that changed must be attached to 1040-X as a "corrected" version. If Schedule C changed, attach new Schedule C. If Schedule D changed, attach new Schedule D. Payment or refund line. Line 22 refund; Line 20 amount you owe. Processing timelines what to actually expect E-filed 1040-X (2019+ returns): Acknowledgment: 1–3 days Processing: ~3 weeks Refund direct deposited (if applicable): 1–2 additional weeks Paper 1040-X: Reaches IRS: 5–7 days mail Processing: 16+ weeks (currently 20+ weeks due to backlogs) Refund via paper check: 4–6 additional weeks Complex amendments (K-1 changes, foreign income, prior-year credit adjustments) can extend processing to 6+ months. Tracking via Where's My Amended Return The IRS provides a specific tool for tracking 1040-X status: Where's My Amended Return . What you need: Social Security Number Date of birth ZIP code Status categories: Received. The IRS has your 1040-X in queue. Adjusted. The change has been processed and your account updated. Completed. Any refund has been issued or additional balance has been billed. Data updates once per day, typically overnight. Availability starts about 3 weeks after e-filing or 3–4 weeks after mailing paper. When you DON'T need to file 1040-X Some errors get fixed automatically by IRS without you needing to amend: Math errors: The IRS recalculates simple math errors and sends a CP notice showing correction. Just verify and, if agreed, no action needed. Missing W-2 or 1099 that IRS already has: If IRS's data matches shows more income than you reported, you'll get a CP2000 notice. You can either agree (pay additional tax) or dispute no 1040-X required if you agree. Missing forms attached to original return: If you forgot to attach a schedule but amounts are correctly reported on 1040, IRS may request missing form without requiring an amendment. Simple withholding amount corrections: Sometimes IRS's W-2 records show different withholding than your return they'll adjust from their records and issue any additional refund. For anything that changes your actual tax liability (income, deductions, credits, filing status), you must file 1040-X. Amending to change filing status Single → MFJ: Allowed if amendment is within 3-year window and you were legally married at year-end. Straightforward. MFS → MFJ. Allowed within 3 years of LATER filing date of either spouse. Common for spouses who initially filed MFS to preserve refund allocation and then decide to combine. MFJ → MFS:" NOT allowed after original filing deadline. Once you elect joint filing, you're locked in for that year (with narrow exceptions for injured spouse or innocent spouse relief). Single → Head of Household: Allowed within 3 years if you meet HoH tests (unmarried, paid >50% of household costs, qualifying dependent). Death of a spouse Qualifying Surviving Spouse status: Available for 2 years following year of death. Amend if you incorrectly filed Single instead. Common 1040-X mistakes Filing before original return is fully processed: The IRS system needs original in its records before it can process an amendment. If you e-filed original 3 days ago, wait 3+ weeks before amending. Not attaching corrected schedule: A 1040-X changing Schedule C net profit must include revised Schedule C. Otherwise IRS can't verify Column B change. Amending state without amending federal: Federal is master record. Amend federal first, then use federal 1040-X as evidence when amending your state return. Filing multiple 1040-Xs for same year simultaneously: File one 1040-X covering all changes for a given year. Multiple pending amendments for same year confuse IRS system. Forgetting explanation in Part III: IRS reviewers rely on Part III to understand change. A blank or generic ("Corrected error") explanation slows processing dramatically. Missing statute of limitations: Amendments filed after 3 years can't claim a refund. Track your 3-year deadlines for open amendments especially if waiting for a resolution on an audit or CP notice. Amending Form 941 with 1040-X: Wrong form. 1040-X amends individual income tax returns only. Employer payroll returns use Form 941-X . Business returns use Form 1120-X, 1120-S-X, or 1065-X. Interest on refunds and owed balances Refunds: The IRS pays interest on 1040-X refunds if refund is issued more than 45 days after you filed amendment. Current rate is ~8% APR. Owed balances: Interest accrues from original due date of return, not from when you filed amendment. Late-payment penalty (0.5% per month) applies on top of interest if balance isn't paid promptly. If your amendment reveals additional tax owed, pay balance with 1040-X (via check, Direct Pay , or EFTPS) to stop penalty clock. Conclusion Form 1040-X is safety net for every mistake on a prior tax return. Three-year window, e-file for 2019+ returns, and Where's My Amended Return for status tracking. The biggest risk isn't amendment itself it's discovering error too late and blowing statute. Frequently asked questions Can I amend a return I already amended? Yes. File another 1040-X. Second amendments must be filed by paper e-file only supports first amendment per tax year. How many years back can I amend? 3 years for refund claims. You can amend older returns to REPORT changes, but you can't receive refunds beyond 3-year window. Does filing 1040-X restart audit clock? No. The audit statute (also 3 years) runs from original filing date, not amendment date. However, amendments filed close to audit deadline may extend audit review if IRS is still examining. What if my original refund was already paid? The 1040-X reconciles against original refund. If amendment reduces your refund, you owe back excess. If it increases refund, you receive additional amount. Can I use same tax software to amend? Yes, most tax software supports 1040-X in same product. Software prepares Column A (original), you enter Column C (corrected), and it calculates Column B (change) automatically. Do I need to send original 1040 with 1040-X? No. The IRS has your original filing. Only send 1040-X + corrected schedules + supporting documents. Can I amend to claim a credit I missed? Yes. Missed QBI deduction , Earned Income Credit, education credit, Retirement Savings Contributions Credit all can be added via 1040-X within 3-year window. What about state income tax on amended return? Amend your state return separately using state's amended-return form (varies by state). Some states have a 4-year statute of limitations, longer than federal.

summary: JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Proficient Auto Logistics, Inc. (NASDAQ: PAL) (the “Company” or “Proficient”), a leading provider of auto transportation and logistics services, today announced the pricing of its previously announced offering of $75.0 million aggregate
body_text: Proficient Auto Logistics Announces Pricing of $75 Million Convertible Bond Offering August 11, 2026 PDF Version JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Proficient Auto Logistics, Inc. (NASDAQ: PAL) (the “Company” or “Proficient”), a leading provider of auto transportation and logistics services, today announced the pricing of its previously announced offering of $75.0 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2033 (the “notes”) in a private offering (the “offering”) to persons reasonably believed to be “qualified institutional buyers” in reliance on the exemption from registration provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). The issuance and sale of the notes are expected to settle on August 13, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The notes will be senior, unsecured obligations of Proficient and will accrue interest at a rate of 5.50% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on February 15 and August 15 of each year, beginning on February 15, 2027. The notes will mature on August 15, 2033, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed or converted. Before May 15, 2033, noteholders will have the right to convert their notes only upon the occurrence of certain events. From and after May 15, 2033, noteholders may convert their notes at any time at their election until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date. Proficient will settle conversions by paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of Proficient common stock or a combination of cash and shares of Proficient common stock, at Proficient’s election. The initial conversion ratio is 153.7870 common shares per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $6.50 per common share. The initial conversion price represents a premium of approximately 27.50% over the last reported sale price of $5.10 per common share on August 11, 2026. The conversion rate and conversion price will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events. The notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations), for cash at Proficient’s option at any time, and from time to time, on or after August 15, 2030 and on or before the 60th scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, but only if the last reported sale price per common share exceeds 130% of the conversion price for a specified period of time and certain other conditions are satisfied. In addition, the notes will be redeemable, in whole and not in part, at Proficient’s option if (i) certain changes in tax law occur; or (ii) the principal amount of the notes outstanding is less than 10% of the aggregate principal amount of notes initially issued, in each case, subject to certain conditions. The redemption price will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date. If a “fundamental change” occurs, then, subject to a limited exception, Proficient will offer to repurchase the notes for cash. The repurchase price will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the applicable repurchase date. Proficient estimates that the net proceeds from the offering will be approximately $71.4 million, after deducting Proficient’s estimated offering expenses. Proficient intends to use the net proceeds from the offering to refinance outstanding indebtedness and to pay the premiums with respect to the capped call transactions described below. In connection with the pricing of the notes, Proficient entered into privately negotiated capped call transactions with certain financial institutions (the “option counterparties”). The capped call transactions are expected generally to reduce potential dilution to Proficient’s common stock upon any conversion of the notes, and/or offset any potential cash payments Proficient is required to make in excess of the principal amount of such converted notes, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap based on the cap price. The cap price of the capped call transactions will initially be $8.93 per share, and is subject to certain adjustments under the terms of the capped call transactions. Unless terminated early or extended, the capped call transactions are expected to expire over a period of trading days beginning on May 18, 2033. Proficient has been advised that, in connection with establishing its initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to purchase shares of Proficient common stock and/or enter into various derivative transactions with respect to Proficient’s common stock concurrently with, or shortly after, the pricing of the notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of Proficient’s common stock or the notes at that time. In addition, the option counterparties and/or their respective affiliates may modify their hedge positions by selling or purchasing Proficient’s common stock or other securities of Proficient in secondary market transactions and/or entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to Proficient’s common stock following the pricing of the notes and prior to the maturity of the notes (and are likely to do so (x) on each exercise date for the capped call transactions, which are expected to occur on each trading day during the 60 trading day period beginning on May 18, 2033 and (y) following any early conversion of the notes, any repurchase of the notes by Proficient on any fundamental change repurchase date, any redemption date or may do so on any other date on which the notes are repurchased by Proficient). This activity could also cause or avoid a decrease or increase in the market price of Proficient’s common stock or the notes, which could affect the ability of noteholders to convert the notes and, to the extent the activity occurs following conversion or during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, it could affect the number of shares and/or value of the consideration that noteholders will receive upon conversion of the notes. The notes and the common stock issuable upon conversion of the notes, if any, have not been and will not be registered under the Securities Act, or any state securities laws, and unless so registered, may not be offered or sold in the United States except pursuant to an applicable exemption from such registration requirements. This announcement is neither an offer to sell nor a solicitation of an offer to buy any of the notes or any shares of common stock potentially issuable upon conversion of the notes and shall not constitute an offer, solicitation or sale in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale is unlawful. About Proficient Auto Logistics – Headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, Proficient Auto Logistics (NASDAQ: PAL) is the leading specialized freight company focused on providing auto transportation and logistics services. Through the combination of nine industry-leading operating companies, including four since IPO debut May 2024, PAL operates the largest auto transportation fleet in North America, offering a broad range of services primarily focused on transporting finished vehicles from automotive production facilities, marine ports of entry, and regional rail yards to auto dealerships around North America. body_text: TL;DR Openmart is the fastest way to pull HVAC company owner contacts filtered by revenue and company size, drawing from a pre-verified database of 200M+ local businesses that refreshes weekly. You skip the live-crawl guesswork and get a clean, revenue-filtered list in minutes. Openmart (top pick) gives you verified HVAC owner contacts filtered by revenue, with 97-99% accuracy and self-serve pricing from $105/mo. Apollo.io works well for larger, multi-location HVAC accounts, but its revenue data thins out on small private operators. ZoomInfo brings strong intent data on bigger companies, at enterprise cost and contract length. Clay lets you build custom enrichment workflows, if you want to configure and maintain them yourself. Core tradeoff: pre-verified database accuracy beats live-web-crawl freshness once you scale outreach. Why revenue filtering is hard for HVAC leads Picture an equipment financing rep staring at a list of 500 HVAC contractors, tasked with prioritizing the ones large enough to finance a $200,000 rooftop unit order. Nearly all of them are privately held, locally owned, and legally required to report revenue nowhere. No SEC filing, no press release, no public firmographic feed carries their numbers. That absence is exactly why sorting HVAC owners by size defeats most B2B data tools. Generic contact databases were built around employees and decision-makers at companies large enough to appear in corporate data feeds. A three-truck HVAC shop doing $1.2M a year rarely shows up cleanly, so its revenue field comes back empty or wildly wrong. Live-crawl pitches promise to fix this by searching the web per lead, but they inherit their own accuracy problem at scale. Two approaches compete to solve this, and the rest of this article evaluates both. One relies on a pre-verified, refreshed database of local business owners. The other sends AI agents to crawl the live web for each contractor on demand. Quick comparison: Openmart vs. Apollo vs. ZoomInfo vs. Clay Here is how the five tools stack up on the one job that matters here: pulling a revenue-filtered list of HVAC company owners you can actually reach. Tool Fit for revenue-based HVAC filtering Data freshness / accuracy Pricing entry Best for Openmart Built to find the owner behind a local SMB Weekly HVAC refresh, 97-99% accuracy, pre-verified $105/mo (Starter, annual) Vendors who want a clean revenue-filtered owner list in minutes Apollo.io Strong for larger, multi-location HVAC rollups Big corporate coverage, thin on private locals Free tier, paid mid-range Selling to enterprise stakeholders ZoomInfo Firmographics strongest on large companies Deep intent data, weak on small private owners Enterprise contract Larger accounts with intent signals Clay Configurable, no ready-made HVAC list Depends on your enrichment setup Credit / usage-based Teams building their own workflow Origami Finds owners via live web crawl, no pre-built database Real-time but per-lead variance, no verification step Free tier, paid from $29/mo Teams that want a live-search discovery tool Use Openmart if you want a pre-verified, revenue-filtered list of local HVAC owners without building anything. Choose Apollo or ZoomInfo if your targets are large multi-location operators that show up in corporate feeds. Pick Clay if you have the time to wire up your own enrichment waterfall, and Origami if you prefer live discovery over a ready-made list. The core distinction stays the same across every row. Openmart is built to find the owner behind a local HVAC business, not a corporate contact database aimed at employees at big companies. Live web search vs. a pre-verified database The live-crawl pitch sounds right until you check the numbers a sales team actually cares about. Advocates argue that static databases miss local HVAC owners and that live web search fixes the gap by pulling fresh data at query time. Freshness is real, but crawling each lead on demand means every contact goes through its own extraction, and the quality of any single record depends on what the crawler happened to find that moment. One owner's email parses cleanly, and the next comes back with a stale listing or a generic office line. A pre-verified database avoids that variance because the work of confirming each contact already happened before you ran the filter. Openmart verifies records against its 200M+ local business database and refreshes HVAC data weekly, so you get both current information and consistent per-lead accuracy across the whole list. You apply a revenue and company-size filter, and every row in the export has already cleared the same verification bar. The difference shows up in deliverability. A B2B SaaS vendor selling to HVAC, plumbing, and home-service businesses ran scraped lists and saw bounce rates between 18% and 25%, high enough to threaten sender reputation. After switching to Openmart's verified contacts, bounces dropped to 3-5%. Cold email reply rates landed at 5-8%, and tighter regional campaigns reached 8-12%. Weekly refresh gives you the freshness the live-crawl narrative promises, and pre-verification gives you the accuracy live crawling can't guarantee lead by lead. For a revenue-filtered HVAC list you want to email this week, you need both. Recommendation If you sell equipment financing, insurance, wholesale supply, or field-service software into the HVAC vertical, Openmart is the fastest path to a revenue-filtered owner list. Openmart targets the owner behind the local business, refreshes HVAC data weekly, and holds 97-99% accuracy, so your reps skip the bounce rates and crawl variance that sink scraped and live-search lists. Start on the Starter plan at $105/mo , filter your target market by estimated revenue and company size, and export a clean list of HVAC owner contacts in minutes. You get a ready-to-use prospecting list without building a live-crawl workflow or waiting on an enterprise contract, which lets you prioritize outreach the same day you sign up. Openmart estimates revenue for private HVAC companies using signals like employee count, number of locations, service area, and business type rather than public financial filings. See the full HVAC leads database for the fields available on export. Openmart applies these signals across our 200M+ local business database to score companies most vendors can't find in corporate data feeds. You get a revenue and size range accurate enough to prioritize a list of contractors for outreach. How often does Openmart refresh HVAC data? Openmart refreshes its HVAC data weekly. Weekly refreshes keep contact details and firmographics current without the per-lead variance of live web crawling. Your exported list reflects recent changes while staying consistent across every record. Does Openmart integrate with a CRM? Openmart does not offer native CRM syncs. You export revenue-filtered HVAC owner lists as clean files and import them into whatever outreach tool or CRM you already use. The export stays crawl-free and verified, so your data lands ready to send. How does pricing scale with list size? Openmart pricing starts at $105 per month on the annual Starter plan, and higher tiers raise your monthly credit and export limits. Larger revenue-filtered lists draw from a bigger credit pool. title: Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises, Inc. announced its financial results for the second quarter of 2026.
body_text: Back Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results Posted August 10, 2026 Revenue in the second quarter of $319.7 million, a 130% increase compared to the same period of 2025, ahead of consensus street expectations Net Income was $14.3 million in the second quarter, compared to a net loss of $58.5 million in the same period of 2025, ahead of consensus street expectations Earnings per share of $0.07, compared to a loss per share of $0.63 in the second quarter of 2025 Adjusted EBITDA in the second quarter of $21.8 million, a 57% increase compared to the same period of 2025, ahead of consensus street expectations Bookings of $151.0 million in the second quarter, a 38% increase compared to the same period of 2025 Backlog of $2.6 billion in the second quarter, a 533% increase compared to the same period of 2025 Secured an additional 1 gigawatt of steam turbines from Siemens Energy for fast delivery in anticipation of our next data center project Total global pipeline exceeds $14.0 billion Announced authorized share repurchase program of up to $50 million Announced repurchase of remaining $61.8 million of outstanding bonds due December 2026 in August 2026 Q2 2026 Financial Highlights and Outlook Revenue of $319.7 million, compared to revenue of $138.9 million in the second quarter of 2025 Net income of $14.3 million, compared to a net loss of $58.5 million in the second quarter of 2025 Adjusted Net Income, which excludes non-cash warrants and other stock costs, was $9.1 million in the second quarter Earnings per share of $0.07, compared to a loss per share of $0.63 in the second quarter of 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $21.8 million, compared to adjusted EBITDA of $13.9 million in the second quarter of 2025 Company raises full year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA target range to $80.0 million to $105.0 million (AKRON, Ohio – August 10, 2026) – Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises, Inc. ("B&W", "Babcock & Wilcox" or the "Company") (NYSE: BW) announced its financial results for the second quarter of 2026. "During the second quarter of 2026, we delivered strong operating results while displaying continued core business momentum, as second quarter revenue, net income and Adjusted EBITDA exceeded Company and consensus street expectations. The growing need for reliable electricity from AI data centers, utilities, industrial customers and expanding economies is accelerating investment in power generation capacity, driving strong demand for our core parts and services, environmental technologies as well as coal and natural gas-fired generation solutions,” commented Kenneth Young, B&W’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. "We continue active discussions on other AI data center opportunities and have placed additional orders with Siemens Energy to secure and deliver an additional 1 gigawatt of steam turbines in the next 12 to 15 months to secure speed to markets. This increase in global energy demand positions us for sustained success across our higher-margin Global Parts and Services business and provides B&W with a strong outlook for the second half of 2026 and beyond. Continued execution of our strategic objectives is delivering results, positioning B&W to capitalize on strong global demand for baseload generation and behind-the-meter data center projects." "Additionally, our first data center project with Base Electron is progressing ahead of expectations and on budget, and manufacturing of the boilers and steam turbines and other long-lead-time components are progressing quickly. The permitting process is underway as we work to provide our proven natural gas-fired boilers and related technologies, alongside Siemens Energy steam turbine systems. This progression with Base Electron further demonstrates our ability to rapidly deploy power solutions, which is a key differentiator that enhances our competitive position in pursuing other data center opportunities." "During the second quarter of 2026, our strong financial results included meaningful growth in net income as well as robust development of our bookings and backlog. As our business expands, we continue hiring in our engineering, business and project development organizations as well as increasing availability of qualified skilled welders and electricians. We are continuing to experience positive momentum at B&W, as we continue to convert our global pipeline of identified project opportunities. In July, we announced that our Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program of up to $50 million, which reflects confidence in our balance sheet and our strategic approach to building shareholder value. In addition, we have raised the upper end of our 2026 Adjusted EBITDA target range to $80.0 million to $105.0 million, reflecting the continued momentum across our business and confidence in additional opportunities ahead. We remain intently focused on our strategic vision and remain optimistic that we will continue to execute on our existing pipeline while maintaining viability for future expansion as we move forward." Q2 2026 Financial Summary Revenues in the second quarter of 2026 were $319.7 million versus revenues of $138.9 million in the second quarter of 2025, primarily driven by an increase in large project volume, including $100.7 million from Base Electron. Operating income in the second quarter of 2026 was $11.8 million, compared to operating income of $7.0 million in the second quarter of 2025. Net income in the second quarter of 2026 was $14.3 million, compared to a net loss of $58.5 million in the second quarter of 2025, driven by the improvement in the operating income results. We benefited from a reduction to interest expense of $6.0 million, change in fair value of customer warrants of $5.9 million and a decrease to tax expense of $5.1 million. Earnings per share in the second quarter of 2026 was $0.07 compared to a loss per share of $0.63 in the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $21.8 million, an increase compared to $13.9 million in the second quarter of 2025. Reconciliations of the non-GAAP measures of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted net income (loss) to the most directly comparable GAAP measures are provided in the exhibits to this release. See “Bookings and Backlog” below for important information regarding our calculation and presentation of those metrics. Liquidity and Balance Sheet At June 30, 2026, the Company had secured debt and bonds of $239.8 million, and a cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash balance of $382.8 million. During the quarter B&W announced the repurchase of the remaining $61.8 million of outstanding December 2026 bonds in August 2026. Earnings Call Information B&W plans to host a conference call and webcast on Monday, August 10, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET to discuss the Company's second quarter 2026 results. The listen-only audio of the conference call will be broadcast live via the Internet on B&W’s Investor Relations site. The dial-in number for participants in the U.S. is (833) 461-5787; the dial-in number for participants in Canada is (365) 657-4084; the dial-in number for participants in all other locations is (585) 542-9983. The conference ID for all participants is 808869498. A replay of this conference call will remain accessible in the investor relations section of the Company’s website for a limited time. Non-GAAP Financial Measures The Company uses non-GAAP financial measures internally, also referred to in this release as “adjusted” financial measures, to evaluate its performance and in making financial and operational decisions. When viewed in conjunction with GAAP results and the accompanying reconciliation, the Company believes that its presentation of these measures provides investors with greater transparency and a greater understanding of factors affecting its financial condition and results of operations than GAAP measures alone. The presentation of non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the Company’s related financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis is a non-GAAP metric and is calculated as earnings before interest expense, tax, depreciation and amortization adjusted for items such as gains or losses arising from the sale of non-income producing assets, net pension benefits, stock-based compensation, restructuring activities, impairments, gains and losses on debt extinguishment, legal and settlement costs, and costs related to financial consulting. In addition, the Company presents consolidated Adjusted EBITDA because it believes it is useful to investors to help facilitate comparisons of the ongoing, operating performance before overhead and other expenses not attributable to the operating performance of the Company. The Company also presents the non-GAAP financial measure of adjusted net income, which excludes $(5.2) million of non-cash warrants and other stock-related costs, as management believes it is a useful measure for investors to accurately reflect the impact of recent stock price growth on costs related to customer warrants and stock-based compensation. This release also presents certain targets for the Company's Adjusted EBITDA in the future; these targets are not intended as guidance regarding how the Company believes the business will perform. The Company is unable to reconcile these targets to their GAAP counterparts without unreasonable effort and expense. Prior period results have been revised to conform with the revised definition and present separate reconciling items in our reconciliation, including business transition costs. Bookings and Backlog Bookings and backlog are our measures of remaining performance obligations under our sales contracts. It is possible that our methodology for determining bookings and backlog may not be comparable to methods used by other companies. We generally include expected revenue from contracts in our backlog when we receive written confirmation from our customers authorizing the performance of work and committing the customers to payment for work performed. Backlog may not be indicative of future operating results, and contracts in our backlog may be canceled, modified or otherwise altered by customers. Backlog can vary significantly from period to period, particularly when large new-build projects or operations and maintenance contracts are booked because they may be fulfilled over multiple years. Because we operate globally, our backlog is also affected by changes in foreign currencies each period. We do not include orders of our unconsolidated joint ventures in backlog. Bookings represent changes to the backlog. Bookings include additions from booking new business, subtractions from customer cancellations or modifications, changes in estimates of liquidated damages that affect selling price and revaluation of backlog denominated in foreign currency. We believe comparing bookings on a quarterly basis or for periods less than one year is less meaningful than for longer periods and that shorter-term changes in bookings may not necessarily indicate a material trend. Pipeline Pipeline represents our uncontracted, potential opportunities, which have been identified and are in active discussions, that could reach a decision to proceed over the next 36 months. Pipeline is an internal metric monitored by management to understand the anticipated growth of our Company and our estimated future revenue, which may increase or decrease from time to time. We cannot guarantee that our pipeline will result in actual revenue in the originally anticipated period or at all. Pipeline may not generate margins equal to our historical operating results. Our customers may experience project delays or cancel orders as a result of external market factors and economic or other factors beyond our control. If our pipeline fails to result in revenue as anticipated or in a timely manner, we could experience a reduction in revenue, profitability, and liquidity. Impacts of Market Conditions Management continues to adapt to macroeconomic conditions, including the impacts from inflation, changing interest rates and foreign exchange rate volatility, current and potential tariff actions, geopolitical conflicts (including the ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East), and global shipping and supply chain disruptions that continued to have an impact across 2026. In certain instances, these situations have resulted in cost increases and delays or disruptions that have had, and could continue to have, an adverse impact on our ability to meet customers’ demands. Additionally, an increase in power demand has caused a shortfall in skilled labor, such as welders and electricians. These labor constraints increase construction costs and affected productivity. To the extent these conditions persist, they may adversely impact future project execution and operating results. We continue to actively monitor the impact of these market conditions on current and future periods and actively manage costs and our liquidity position to provide additional flexibility while still supporting our customers and their specific needs. The duration and scope of these conditions cannot be predicted, and therefore, any anticipated negative financial impact on our operating results cannot be reasonably estimate.
