title: Top 8 Leading AI Platforms for Automated Outreach in 2026
summary: Looking for AI outreach software? Compare Trellus, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, Smartlead, Lemlist, Klenty, and Snov.io in one mega detailed guide. Read on...
body_text: Finding prospects. Researching companies. Writing personalized emails. Logging calls. Updating CRMs. Deciding who deserves another follow up. All of those tasks consume hours every week. The result is something every sales leader has seen before. Reps spend half the day preparing to sell and far less time having conversations that generate revenue. That is exactly where the new generation of leading AI platforms for automated outreach has found its place. Thanks to the way technology has advanced over the last couple of years, especially the AI aspect, because that’s been more of a stepping stone, we’ve got tons of solutions right now. Needless to say, mere “Outreach” isn’t the issue anymore. You could slap a bunch of messages and send them through an automated outreach software, but that won’t get the job done. It requires personalization, a bunch of tweaks and background research for you to see any modicum of conversions, but we’ll get to that later in detail. For now, let’s say you are conceptually asking What are the best AI platforms for automated outreach in 2026? The answer depends on how your team sells. A startup booking twenty demos every month needs something very different from a global sales organization running hundreds of outbound campaigns across multiple markets. Some teams care about massive contact databases. Others need AI coaching during live conversations. Then there’s the remote sales team aspect that may need just better overall communication without any near misses. The difficult part worth noting in these situations is separating products with genuinely useful AI from platforms that simply added "AI" to their marketing pages. Without further ado, we’re going for a detailed drill down of the best leading AI platforms that are hot right now for outreach, sales and workflow optimization. Along the way, we'll also answer questions like: How do AI outreach platforms improve response rates and booking rates? Can AI automate outreach while maintaining personalization and authenticity? Which AI outreach platforms work across email, phone, and LinkedIn? How to implement AI outreach automation without losing the human touch? If your outbound team wants more conversations without hiring twice as many SDRs, you're in exactly the right place. What Makes an AI Automated Outreach Tool Different From Traditional Sales Software? Focus on the “automation” part, and that pretty much sums it up for you. Automated outreach software is a counterpart of traditional programs that were used for contacting prospects. The main difference is that automation has helped to improve a bunch of different things, in a good sense, of course. It has completely eliminated or minimized time and resource allocation around prospect research, personalized messaging, appropriate time to call someone, prioritization or deprioritization of accounts, workflow management, and vice versa. Modern Automated prospecting and outreach software changes different things aside from workflow in more of an end to end optimization manner. You are looking at better scaling, numbers, performance, and other things too, besides outreach. If prospects consistently reply on Tuesday mornings, many modern systems begin prioritizing those send windows automatically. If one messaging style outperforms another across hundreds of campaigns, AI adjusts future recommendations. According to Salesforce's State of Sales research, cited by ADAI News , 83 percent of sales teams already use AI or plan to adopt AI tools within the next twelve months. That number tells a much bigger story than software adoption. Outbound sales have entered a completely different era. Types of AI Outreach Software Yes, you guessed it right. There are multiple types of digital solutions that people use daily. Some of them are partly automated, while others come with full on automated features, alongside the usual deliverables that are part of the tech stack. Understanding the major categories helps narrow your search much faster. Enterprise Sales Engagement Platforms Large sales organizations typically need much more than email sequencing. They require forecasting, territory management, conversation intelligence, AI coaching, advanced reporting, permission controls, CRM synchronization, and support for thousands of active opportunities. Enterprise platforms combine all those capabilities inside one ecosystem. Products like Outreach.io and Salesloft dominate this segment because they were designed for organizations managing large outbound teams across multiple regions. These platforms make sense when multiple departments share customer data and every sales activity contributes toward larger revenue forecasts. For smaller businesses, the investment can become difficult to justify. The software is powerful, although many startups never use enough features to recover the higher subscription costs. CRM Native Outreach Platforms Many companies prefer keeping every customer interaction inside the CRM their sales team already uses every day. CRM native solutions follow that philosophy. Rather than forcing sales representatives to jump between several applications, outreach becomes part of the existing workflow. Activities, conversations, follow ups, contact records, and reporting stay synchronized automatically. That reduces administrative work and minimizes duplicate data. The trade off is flexibility. Once your outreach process depends heavily on one CRM ecosystem, changing platforms later becomes a much larger project. Data Plus Sequencing Platforms These products combine prospect databases with outbound execution. Sales representatives search millions of contacts using company size, industry, technology stack, hiring activity, intent signals, funding events, and dozens of other filters. Once the ideal audience has been identified, campaigns launch immediately without exporting spreadsheets between separate applications. Apollo has become one of the strongest examples of this category because it combines contact intelligence with sequencing, CRM capabilities, AI research, and calling inside one workspace. Teams looking for efficient prospecting often find tremendous value here because every stage of the outbound process happens inside one interface. AI First Outreach Platforms A newer category has emerged over the last couple of years. These platforms place artificial intelligence at the center of the workflow instead of adding AI features onto existing software. Their emphasis extends beyond email generation. Many combine Conversational AI for sales outreach , live coaching, AI dialing, conversation intelligence, personalized messaging, workflow automation, and predictive recommendations throughout every stage of outbound sales. Several also include AI voice and messaging automation tools that help sales representatives handle larger call volumes while maintaining personalized conversations. For organizations looking to maximize selling time, this category has become increasingly attractive because the AI assists before, during, and after every customer interaction. Platform Best For AI Highlights Channels Ideal Team 🥇 Trellus AI outbound calling & sales enablement Parallel Dialing, Live AI Coaching, Practice Calls, Conversation Intelligence, Workflow Automation Phone • LinkedIn • CRM SDRs & Outbound Teams Apollo Prospecting & lead database AI prospect research, Email generation, CRM, Contact intelligence Email • Calls • CRM Startups & SMBs Smartlead Cold email at scale Inbox rotation, AI reply categorization, Campaign automation Email Agencies & Lead Gen Teams Lemlist Personalized outreach AI personalization, Landing pages, Visual emails Email • LinkedIn Relationship Selling Snov.io Affordable outreach AI email writer, Verification, Email warm-up Email Small Businesses Klenty AI sales coaching Live coaching, Action AI, Voicemail detection Email • Phone • LinkedIn • SMS Growing Sales Teams Outreach.io Enterprise sales engagement Forecasting, AI sequence optimization, Conversation Intelligence Email • Phone • CRM Enterprise Organizations Salesloft Revenue teams Deal Intelligence, AI Cadences, Coaching, Pipeline Insights Email • Phone • LinkedIn Enterprise Revenue Teams 1. Trellus: AIO Sales Enablement, Automated Cold Outreach and Conversion Platform Trellus earns the top position among the leading AI platforms for automated outreach for a variety of reasons. We created this platform around a simple observation, i.e. sales representatives do not lose deals because they lack email templates. They lose opportunities because administrative work, context switching, manual dialing, CRM updates, and scattered workflows consume hours that could have been spent talking to buyers. Every minute spent researching an account or logging call notes is a minute that could have been another live conversation. Trellus.ai removes much of that operational friction. It combines intelligent dialing, AI coaching, conversation intelligence, workflow automation, and prospect research inside a single workspace, giving SDRs everything they need without bouncing between five or six browser tabs. For outbound teams measured on meetings booked, conversations started, and pipeline created, that difference becomes obvious very quickly. While many products market themselves as AI powered email and outreach automation , this platform places equal emphasis on phone outreach because conversations still close deals faster than inboxes alone. That makes it particularly attractive for teams running high volume outbound campaigns where speed and consistency matter just as much as personalization. Another strength is how naturally artificial intelligence fits into the selling process. The AI is not trying to replace the salesperson. On the contrary, our technology supports them before the call, during the conversation, and after the meeting ends. Prospecting becomes faster. Calling becomes smarter. Follow ups happen sooner. Managers gain better visibility without asking every representative to complete another spreadsheet. For companies searching for Automated prospecting and outreach software that keeps human conversations at the center of outbound sales, few platforms feel as purpose built. Best features Before looking at the highlights below, it is worth understanding why these capabilities matter together. Many competitors offer one or two AI features. Few connect prospecting, calling, coaching, and workflow automation into a single experience. That connected workflow reduces context switching, shortens administrative work, and allows representatives to remain focused on selling. AI Parallel Dialing Sales representatives spend an incredible amount of time waiting. Waiting for calls to connect. Waiting through voicemail. Waiting for unanswered numbers. Parallel dialing changes that equation. The platform intelligently works through multiple prospects, helping representatives reach more live conversations during every calling block without sacrificing compliance or visibility. For outbound teams measured on activity and meetings booked, this alone can transform daily productivity. The main downside to parallel dialing is that numbers are called simultaneously, so you never know who will pick up the call first. Therefore, have your research notes and script ready because you DO NOT want to mess up a high ticket call on parallel dialing. Real Time AI Sales Coaching Coaching becomes valuable when it happens during the conversation, not three days later. The AI analyzes live calls and provides guidance that helps representatives navigate objections, maintain momentum, and handle difficult moments with greater confidence. New hires ramp faster because experienced coaching becomes available from day one. Managers also spend less time correcting repeated mistakes after the fact. AI Practice/ Mock Calls Every SDR remembers how uncomfortable the first cold calls felt. Practice environments solve that problem. Representatives can rehearse conversations against AI personas that simulate realistic buyer responses, helping them build confidence before speaking with actual prospects. It creates a safer learning environment while improving consistency across the sales organization. LinkedIn Superhuman Researching prospects often consumes more time than contacting them. This feature surfaces relevant account information while representatives browse LinkedIn, helping them personalize outreach without opening multiple research tools. Small productivity improvements like this compound throughout the day. Conversation Intelligence Every customer interaction contains valuable information. The platform captures those insights automatically, helping managers identify successful messaging, common objections, coaching opportunities, and performance patterns across the team. That visibility becomes increasingly valuable as outbound organizations grow. Workflow Automation Administrative work quietly steals selling time. Follow up reminders, activity logging, CRM synchronization, and repetitive tasks happen automatically, allowing representatives to stay focused on customer conversations instead of operational work. Pros Before comparing strengths, remember that every outbound organization measures success differently. Some prioritize conversation volume. Others emphasize coaching quality or workflow efficiency. The advantages below make the platform especially attractive for sales teams focused on pipeline generation. AI powered parallel dialing helps representatives reach significantly more live prospects during every calling session. Real time coaching supports sales conversations while they are happening, helping SDRs improve performance without waiting for manager feedback. Practice calls create a realistic training environment that shortens onboarding and accelerates ramp time for new hires. LinkedIn research tools reduce preparation time while making personalization easier for every outbound campaign. Conversation intelligence provides managers with actionable coaching insights without reviewing every recording manually. Workflow automation minimizes repetitive administrative work, keeping representatives focused on revenue generating activities. Strong integration with modern sales engagement workflows reduces context switching throughout the workday. 2. Apollo Ask almost any SDR to recommend a prospecting platform and Apollo will appear within the first few answers. That reputation did not happen by accident. Apollo has built one of the largest commercially available prospect databases on the market, giving sales teams access to hundreds of millions of contacts alongside sequencing, CRM functionality, meeting scheduling, enrichment, and AI assistance. For many companies, it becomes the first serious investment after spreadsheets stop being enough. The biggest attraction is convenience. Prospect discovery, account research, email sequences, calling, and engagement tracking all happen inside one platform. There is very little exporting and importing between separate tools, which keeps the outbound workflow moving. Its AI capabilities have matured considerably over the past couple of years. The built in assistant can recommend prospects, summarize accounts, generate personalized messaging, suggest follow ups, and help launch campaigns through a conversational interface. For busy SDRs, that removes a surprising amount of repetitive work every single day. That makes Apollo one of the strongest examples of Intelligent lead engagement platforms currently available. It also combines data with execution, giving representatives both the audience and the tools needed to start conversations. Still, there are a few trade offs worth understanding before committing. The credit system works well during moderate prospecting activity. Large outbound teams can burn through allocations much faster than expected, especially when running multiple campaigns across several representatives. Mailbox limits are another consideration. Organizations managing very large email operations may eventually outgrow those restrictions and begin looking elsewhere. Why sales teams choose Apollo The biggest selling point remains simplicity. Many companies purchase separate products for prospect data, email sequencing, CRM management, enrichment, and meeting scheduling. Apollo combines those functions under one subscription. That reduces software costs while creating a smoother workflow for outbound representatives. The AI assistant also deserves attention. Finding prospects used to involve applying filters one by one, opening profiles, researching accounts, and writing outreach manually. Now much of that work can happen through conversational prompts. That productivity gain becomes increasingly valuable as outbound teams scale. If your primary question is Can AI automate outreach while maintaining personalization and authenticity? , Apollo demonstrates that it can, provided representatives still review and refine AI generated messaging before sending. Blind automation rarely performs as well as thoughtful personalization supported by AI. 3. Smartlead If your sales organization measures success by the number of campaigns running simultaneously, Smartlead deserves serious attention. Many outreach platforms were designed around one sales team working from one company. Smartlead was built with agencies and large outbound operations in mind. That difference becomes obvious within the first few minutes of using it. Managing multiple clients usually means managing multiple domains, dozens of inboxes, different sending schedules, separate reply handling rules, and completely different campaign strategies. Keeping all of that organized manually quickly becomes exhausting. Smartlead simplifies that workload through automation. Its biggest strength is large scale inbox management. The platform allows teams to connect a very high number of mailboxes while automatically rotating sending activity across accounts. That helps distribute email volume naturally, protecting sender reputation and reducing the chances of one mailbox carrying all the risk. For agencies handling outreach on behalf of several clients, this alone can remove hours of repetitive operational work every week. It also includes AI that categorizes incoming replies into meaningful groups. Positive replies, objections, unsubscribe requests, automatic responses, and neutral conversations are organized automatically, allowing sales teams to prioritize the conversations that deserve immediate attention. That makes Smartlead one of the stronger AI powered email and outreach automation platforms for organizations where campaign scale is more important than individual personalization. Where opinions become more divided is the writing quality. The AI performs well for creating structured cold emails, but many experienced SDRs still rewrite large portions before launching campaigns. The messaging often feels generic, especially when targeting executive buyers who receive dozens of cold emails every day. Why agencies gravitate toward Smartlead Running outreach for one business is manageable. Running outreach for ten clients at the same time is an entirely different operational problem. Every client has separate branding, different domains, unique messaging, independent reporting, and different campaign objectives. Without automation, inbox management alone becomes a full time job. Smartlead removes much of that administrative burden. Campaigns remain organized, mailboxes stay healthier, and teams spend more time optimizing outreach instead of maintaining infrastructure. That operational efficiency explains why many lead generation agencies consider it one of the strongest Automated prospecting and outreach software options available today. Pros Before looking through the highlights below, remember that Smartlead was built primarily for scale. Companies sending a few hundred emails each week may never use many of these capabilities. Large outbound operations, however, will appreciate the flexibility. Supports a very large number of mailbox connections, making high volume outreach much easier to manage. AI automatically categorizes replies according to intent, helping sales representatives focus on promising conversations first. Built specifically for agencies managing multiple client campaigns from one workspace. Strong deliverability controls through intelligent mailbox rotation. Campaign management remains organized even across large outbound teams. Simple interface makes campaign deployment relatively straightforward despite the platform's scale. Cons Every platform makes trade offs. Smartlead focuses heavily on campaign infrastructure, leaving room for improvement in several areas. AI generated email copy often requires editing before it feels genuinely personalized. Built in prospect database is not as comprehensive as platforms centered around sales intelligence. Native calling capabilities remain limited compared with platforms designed around phone outreach. Reporting can feel basic for organizations looking for deep revenue attribution. 4. Lemlist There was a time when nearly every cold email looked exactly the same. Plain text. Generic introductions. Predictable sales pitches. Recipients learned to ignore them almost instantly. Lemlist built its reputation solving that problem. The platform became well known for visual personalization, allowing sales teams to embed customized images, personalized landing pages, company logos, screenshots, and dynamic elements directly into outreach campaigns. Also Read: Trellus × Lemlist: Turning Outbound Signals Into Real Conversations Those creative touches helped emails stand out in crowded inboxes long before artificial intelligence became part of everyday sales software. Today, AI has expanded those capabilities considerably. The platform now generates personalized opening lines, suggests follow up messaging, researches LinkedIn profiles, and assists with campaign creation while still keeping personalization at the center of the experience. That makes it one of the more creative leading AI platforms for automated outreach available in 2026. If your outbound strategy depends on making memorable first impressions, Lemlist continues to perform extremely well. Personalization extends beyond inserting someone's first name into an email. The AI can reference recent company updates, professional achievements, industry trends, and public information that makes outreach feel considerably more thoughtful. That level of personalization often produces better engagement than sending thousands of generic emails. Still, there are practical considerations. High volume senders may find themselves relying on additional deliverability tools for mailbox warm up and infrastructure management. Some competitors provide stronger built in deliverability systems, reducing the need for external software. The platform also rewards creativity. Sales representatives willing to experiment with visuals, landing pages, and personalized campaigns usually get much more value than teams looking for simple email automation. Why creative sales teams like Lemlist Every buyer receives hundreds of cold emails every month. Standing out matters. Visual personalization creates curiosity before prospects even begin reading the message. That curiosity often translates into higher open rates, stronger engagement, and better reply opportunities. The AI prepares much of that information automatically, allowing sales teams to personalize campaigns across hundreds of prospects without sacrificing relevance. For companies asking How do AI outreach platforms improve response rates and booking rates? , this is one of the strongest examples. Better personalization usually leads to better conversations. Better conversations often produce more meetings. Pros The strengths below explain why Lemlist remains popular among outbound teams focused on relationship building. AI generates personalized introductions using publicly available prospect information. Visual personalization helps emails stand out inside crowded inboxes. Personalized landing pages increase campaign engagement beyond traditional cold emails. LinkedIn data supports richer account research before outreach begins. Multichannel campaigns combine email, LinkedIn, and follow ups inside one workflow. Strong community with extensive educational resources for outbound sales professionals. Cons No outreach platform performs perfectly across every category. These limitations are worth considering before making a purchasing decision. Deliverability infrastructure is not as comprehensive as platforms dedicated primarily to inbox management. Advanced personalization features require more campaign preparation than simpler email tools. Reporting lacks some enterprise level analytics available from larger sales engagement platforms. New users often need time to understand the platform's creative campaign capabilities. 5. Snov.io I'll admit, I underestimated Snov.io the first time I looked at it. The starting price made me skeptical. Many affordable outreach platforms promise an impressive list of features, only for you to discover that the important capabilities sit behind expensive upgrades or usage limits. Snov.io turned out to be more capable than I expected. It combines lead generation, email verification, campaign management, CRM functionality, AI email writing, and prospect tracking inside a single platform. That makes it appealing for startups and growing sales teams that want one subscription covering most of their outbound workflow. The AI writing assistant deserves particular attention. Creating personalized cold emails for hundreds of prospects usually requires significant effort. Snov.io speeds up that process by generating email drafts, subject lines, and follow up sequences based on your prompts. It also supports translation into dozens of languages, making international outreach much easier for companies selling across multiple regions. For businesses building multilingual outbound campaigns, that feature alone can eliminate hours of manual work every week. Another pleasant surprise is the inclusion of unlimited sender accounts and unlimited email warm up across all pricing tiers. Those capabilities are frequently reserved for premium plans elsewhere. Having them available from the beginning makes the platform considerably more attractive for companies planning to scale their outreach over time. That said, Snov.io is not trying to compete with enterprise sales engagement platforms. Its emphasis remains email centric, with LinkedIn automation available as a separate paid add on. If your outbound strategy revolves around coordinated engagement across email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and calling, you may eventually outgrow its core feature set. For organizations primarily interested in AI powered email and outreach automation , however, Snov.io offers excellent value. Pros Before reviewing the highlights below, remember that affordability is only one part of the equation. The platform succeeds because it delivers practical functionality without overwhelming new users. Competitive starting price makes advanced outreach technology accessible for smaller businesses. AI email writer creates personalized cold emails, subject lines, and follow up sequences from simple prompts. Native translation across 36 languages supports international sales campaigns without relying on external translation tools. Unlimited email warm up helps protect sender reputation as outreach volume grows. Unlimited sender accounts allow teams to scale campaigns without immediate infrastructure upgrades. Built in email verification improves deliverability by reducing bounced messages before campaigns launch. Unibox centralizes responses from multiple campaigns into one organized workspace. Cons No platform is perfect, and there are a few areas where buyers should set realistic expectations. LinkedIn automation requires a separate monthly subscription, increasing the total cost for multichannel outreach. Analytics remain fairly basic compared with larger enterprise platforms. Monthly credits expire if unused, which can be frustrating for companies with inconsistent outreach schedules. Contact data quality varies across niche industries and smaller regional markets. Phone outreach capabilities remain limited compared with platforms built around calling. 6. Klenty Klenty surprised me for a completely different reason. I expected another multichannel outreach platform. What caught my attention was how much effort had gone into helping sales representatives during live conversations. Many AI tools focus on preparing emails before the outreach begins. Klenty spends just as much time helping reps once someone finally answers the phone. That matters because booking a meeting rarely depends on sending another email. It depends on handling objections, asking better questions, and keeping conversations moving in the right direction. Klenty's AI coaching system listens to live calls and provides contextual guidance while the conversation is still happening. Battle cards appear automatically. Potential objections are identified in real time. Conversation scorecards begin building before the call even ends. For newer SDRs, it feels almost like having an experienced sales manager sitting quietly beside them throughout every conversation. That coaching capability makes Klenty one of the more interesting Conversational AI for sales outreach platforms available today. The platform also supports multichannel cadences across email, LinkedIn, phone calls, SMS, and WhatsApp. That flexibility allows sales organizations to reach prospects through the communication channels they already use every day. One feature worth paying attention to is Action AI. After a conversation ends, the system automatically triggers the next appropriate activity within the sales cadence. Successful conversation? Schedule the follow up. Voicemail reached? Queue another touchpoint. Prospect requested more information? Move them into the next sequence automatically. Removing those manual decisions saves meaningful time for representatives making dozens of calls every day. Pricing becomes the biggest consideration. As teams grow, per user subscription costs rise quickly, making Klenty more attractive for organizations that value coaching enough to justify the additional investment. For companies wondering How to implement AI outreach automation without losing the human touch? , Klenty provides a compelling answer. Pros The strengths below explain why Klenty continues to build a loyal following among outbound organizations. AI coaching delivers live battle cards, objection detection, and conversation guidance while calls are taking place. Action AI automatically advances prospects through the correct sales cadence after each interaction. Multichannel engagement supports email, LinkedIn, calls, SMS, and WhatsApp from one platform. AI detects voicemail and interactive voice response systems, reducing wasted dialing time. Outcome detection categorizes conversations automatically, simplifying reporting and follow up. CRM synchronization keeps customer records updated without requiring additional administrative work. Customer support consistently receives positive feedback across review platforms. Cons There are still a few limitations worth considering before making a long term commitment. Per user pricing becomes expensive for larger outbound organizations. User interface feels dated compared with several newer competitors. Performance can slow during larger campaigns involving significant contact volumes. CRM synchronization delays occasionally appear in customer reviews. Reporting customization remains limited for revenue operations teams seeking advanced analytics. 7. Outreach.io If you've spent time around enterprise sales teams, you've almost certainly heard Outreach.io mentioned in conversations about sales engagement. The platform has been one of the category leaders for years, and for good reason. Large revenue organizations need far more than email automation. They need accurate forecasting, standardized sales processes, conversation intelligence, coaching, analytics, CRM synchronization, and visibility across hundreds of representatives. That is exactly where Outreach.io performs well. The platform uses artificial intelligence to analyze millions of customer interactions, helping sales teams identify which messaging performs best, when prospects are most likely to engage, and which opportunities deserve immediate attention. Over time, those recommendations become increasingly valuable because they're based on a massive volume of engagement data gathered across enterprise customers. One of the strongest capabilities is sequence optimization. Sales managers spend countless hours experimenting with send times, follow up intervals, subject lines, and messaging variations. Outreach.io continuously analyzes campaign performance and recommends adjustments that can improve engagement over time. That makes it one of the more mature leading AI platforms for automated outreach available today. Conversation intelligence is another major advantage. Every recorded meeting and sales call becomes a learning opportunity. The platform identifies customer sentiment, tracks important discussion topics, surfaces objections, and highlights coaching opportunities for managers. Instead of manually reviewing dozens of recordings every week, leaders can focus on conversations that need attention. That becomes increasingly valuable as sales organizations grow. Where Outreach.io asks for patience is implementation. This is not software most companies purchase on Monday and master before Friday. Enterprise deployments typically involve CRM integration, workflow configuration, permission management, sales process alignment, and extensive onboarding. Organizations willing to invest the time usually gain an exceptionally capable platform. Smaller companies may find the complexity unnecessary for their current stage. It also serves organizations looking for sophisticated AI powered email and outreach automation tied directly to forecasting and revenue operations. Rather than simply measuring email opens and reply rates, Outreach.io connects engagement activity with pipeline progression and sales outcomes. That broader business visibility explains why it remains a popular enterprise choice. Pros Before reviewing the strengths below, remember that Outreach.io was designed for larger organizations with structured sales operations. Many of these capabilities become more valuable as teams grow. AI optimizes outreach sequences using engagement patterns collected across millions of customer interactions. Conversation intelligence delivers sentiment analysis, keyword tracking, coaching insights, and call summaries. Advanced forecasting tools support revenue leaders with better pipeline visibility. Strong CRM integrations with enterprise sales ecosystems. Excellent analytics for measuring team performance across multiple outbound channels. Enterprise grade workflow automation reduces repetitive administrative work. Extensive reporting supports sales leadership, revenue operations, and executive decision making. Cons Large platforms inevitably introduce additional complexity. These considerations are worth evaluating before moving forward. Enterprise pricing places the platform outside the budget of many startups and small businesses. Initial implementation requires planning, onboarding, and internal change management. New users often face a steeper learning curve than lighter outreach platforms. Customization options can feel overwhelming for organizations with simple outbound processes. Smaller teams may never use the platform's full feature set. 8. Salesloft Salesloft has spent years competing directly with Outreach.io, and the competition has pushed both platforms to become considerably stronger. Although they overlap in several areas, Salesloft brings its own philosophy to outbound sales. The platform places significant emphasis on helping representatives execute consistent sales cadences while giving managers deep visibility into performance. Artificial intelligence now supports nearly every stage of that workflow. Email creation, meeting preparation, opportunity insights, conversation summaries, deal risk analysis, and coaching recommendations all benefit from AI assistance. For enterprise organizations managing hundreds of active opportunities, those productivity gains become meaningful very quickly. Salesloft also performs well across multiple communication channels. Representatives can coordinate email, phone, LinkedIn, meetings, and follow ups without constantly switching between disconnected applications. That unified experience creates a smoother workflow and reduces administrative effort throughout the day. One capability that deserves recognition is deal intelligence. The platform analyzes engagement activity across active opportunities, helping managers identify deals showing signs of slowing down before problems become obvious in the pipeline. Early visibility gives sales leaders more time to coach representatives and re engage buyers before opportunities stall completely. Salesloft also continues investing heavily in Conversational AI for sales outreach , helping managers understand how top performers handle conversations and where coaching can improve team performance. The primary consideration remains cost. Like Outreach.io, Salesloft targets enterprise customers. Smaller organizations may struggle to justify the investment unless they expect significant outbound growth. Why large revenue teams choose Salesloft Scaling outbound sales involves much more than increasing activity. Consistency becomes equally important. Managers want every representative following proven workflows. Leadership wants accurate forecasting. Revenue operations wants reliable reporting. Representatives want fewer administrative tasks. Salesloft addresses each of those priorities through one connected platform. Artificial intelligence supports decision making throughout the sales process while allowing representatives to remain focused on customer conversations. For organizations asking Which AI outreach platforms work across email, phone, and LinkedIn? , Salesloft belongs firmly on the shortlist. Its multichannel engagement capabilities continue to rank among the strongest in the enterprise market. Pros Salesloft combines enterprise functionality with mature AI capabilities that continue expanding every year. AI assisted email creation speeds campaign development while maintaining personalization. Strong multichannel engagement across email, phone, LinkedIn, meetings, and follow ups. Conversation intelligence supports coaching and performance improvement. Deal intelligence identifies opportunities requiring immediate attention. Excellent CRM integration with Salesforce and other enterprise ecosystems. Robust analytics and reporting for revenue operations teams. Highly scalable for organizations with growing outbound teams. Cons Like every enterprise platform, there are trade offs that buyers should understand. Premium pricing may exceed the budgets of startups and smaller businesses. Onboarding requires planning and dedicated administrative resources. Some advanced capabilities require additional configuration before teams receive maximum value. Interface can feel overwhelming for new users unfamiliar with enterprise sales engagement platforms. How We Selected These Leading AI Platforms for Automated Outreach There are hundreds of outreach tools claiming to use artificial intelligence. To create this list, we looked beyond marketing claims and focused on how these platforms perform during everyday sales activities. Several factors influenced the rankings. AI capabilities Artificial intelligence should solve meaningful business problems. We looked for platforms that automate repetitive work, improve prospect prioritization, provide useful coaching, enhance personalization, and help representatives spend more time selling. Multichannel outreach Modern outbound sales rarely happens through email alone. The strongest platforms support coordinated engagement across email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and other communication channels whenever appropriate. Ease of adoption Powerful software loses value if sales teams struggle to use it. Platforms received higher consideration when they balanced advanced functionality with an intuitive workflow. Automation depth Basic email sequences are no longer enough. The products included here automate prospect research, follow ups, workflow management, coaching, conversation analysis, or lead prioritization in meaningful ways. Overall value Price always matters. A platform does not need to be the cheapest. It should deliver measurable value relative to its subscription cost and target audience. Go On a Trialing Spree! A lot of things come down to your sales motion and business requirements. Therefore, it’s possible that the software that you’re considering signing up for may not be the perfect fit. We recommend trying different programs on this list through trial plans or basic paid plans to get the lay of the land. Once you have a program that marks all the checkboxes, feel free to onboard your entire sales team and move to a paid tier.

body_text: News Release View printer-friendly version << Back URBAN ONE, INC. REPORTS SECOND QUARTER 2026 RESULTS SILVER SPRING, Md. , Aug. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Urban One, Inc. (NASDAQ: UONEK and UONE, referred to as, "Urban One," the "Company", "we", "our" and/or "us") today reported its results for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the three months ended June 30, 2026, net revenue was approximately $85.8 million, a decrease of 6.4% from the same period in 2025. The Company reported operating loss of approximately $11.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to operating loss of approximately $120.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Broadcast and digital operating income(1) was approximately $22.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, a decrease of $3.5 million from the same period in 2025. Net loss was approximately $7.1 million or $(1.58) per share (basic) for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to net loss of $77.9 million or $(17.41)(a) per share (basic) for the same period in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA(2) was approximately $11.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to approximately $14.0 million for the same period in 2025. Alfred C. Liggins, III, Urban One's CEO and President stated, "We saw some sequential improvement in the second quarter compared to the first quarter, with lower rates of revenue decline. Cable Television was down 7.4%, Digital was down 8.4%, Radio was down 3.9%, and Reach Media dropped by 10.6%. In Radio, our Miller Kaplan local Radio revenues were down 10.1% year-over-year vs. the market down 7.8%; and national was down 1.5% vs. the market down 4.6%. Including local digital, second quarter Radio revenue was down 4.9%. We did approximately $1.4 million in gross political advertising in the second quarter. Radio third quarter is pacing down 2.8%. We remain in a turnaround situation at Reach Media, where we continue to be impacted by a weak marketplace, key client attrition and sales team re-building. We continue to closely manage cash flows from operations, with concerted efforts to collect receivables and manage discretionary vendor spend. During the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company repurchased approximately $23.5 million of its 2031 Second Lien Notes at a weighted average price of approximately 42.0% of par. Year-to-date, that is a total reduction in long-term debt of $60.2 million for an annual interest savings of $4.6 million and an increase in short-term debt of $10.0 million. During the quarter we completed the disposition of WLNK and WMXG in Charlotte. Our revised Adjusted EBITDA(2) guide for 2026 is now in the mid-fifty-million dollar range, given the realities of the current marketplace." FCC approval was obtained on May 13, 2026 for the WMXG station and on May 12, 2026 for the WLNK-FM station. The Company completed both sales on June 1, 2026 and recognized a gain of $4.7 million, which is included in Gain On Sale Of Business in the unaudited consolidated statement of operations for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026. On April 28, 2026, the Company entered into an agreement to acquire Service Broadcasting Group, LLC, including radio stations KKDA and KRNB in Dallas, Texas for $22.0 million. The Company recognized a gain of $3.2 million on the KZMJ disposition in the third quarter of 2026. We recognized approximately $35.3 million of revenue from our Radio Broadcasting segment during the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to approximately $36.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of approximately $1.4 million. This decrease was primarily driven by weaker overall market demand from the national and local advertisers. We recognized approximately $4.8 million of revenue from our Reach Media segment during the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to approximately $5.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of approximately $0.5 million. This decrease was primarily driven by a decrease in syndicated revenue. title: Cash Flow Capital And How It Supports Business Liquidity In 2026
summary: Learn what cash flow capital means, how it relates to working capital, and how businesses can protect liquidity through better receivables, payables, inventory, and spend control.
body_text: Cash flow capital is tested when a business has enough sales activity but not enough liquidity moving through the operating cycle. Revenue may be growing, yet cash can still be trapped in receivables, inventory, supplier commitments, payroll, and recurring operating expenses. This is especially relevant for UAE SMEs. The Central Bank of the UAE’s MSME Business Survey found that only 17% of MSMEs applied for bank credit in 2020 , and only 9% secured the finance needed . The report also identified inadequate liquidity, cash flow constraints, and lack of collateral as reasons why MSMEs struggled to secure bank financing. Cash flow capital, therefore, should not be reduced to a funding question. Before borrowing more, finance teams need to understand where capital is trapped, how quickly receivables convert, when suppliers must be paid, how much inventory is being held, and whether operating spend is quietly increasing the baseline cash requirement. In this blog, we will explain what cash flow capital means in practical terms, how it connects with working capital, and how businesses can protect liquidity by managing the cash cycle more effectively. TL;DR / Key Takeaways Cash flow capital refers to the practical liquidity available to support day-to-day operations while cash moves through the business. It is closely linked to working capital, but it focuses more on timing gaps between collections, supplier payments, inventory, payroll, and operating spend. Revenue growth can increase pressure on cash flow capital when costs rise before customer cash is collected. Receivables, inventory, supplier terms, fixed costs, and recurring spend are the main areas where liquidity gets trapped. Businesses can protect cash flow capital by improving collections, aligning payments, controlling inventory, and keeping operating spend visible. What Cash Flow Capital Means In Practice Cash flow capital is not a formal accounting term found in financial statements. Instead, it is used in a practical sense to describe the capital available to support the movement of cash through a business. It represents the liquidity required to: pay suppliers manage payroll fund inventory cover operating expenses handle timing gaps between inflows and outflows Unlike profit or revenue, which are measured on an accounting basis, cash flow capital reflects the real availability of funds at any point in time. A business may appear strong on paper but still face pressure if cash is tied up in receivables or inventory. This is why understanding cash flow capital requires looking beyond balances and focusing on how quickly cash moves through the operating cycle. How Cash Flow And Working Capital Are Connected Cash flow and working capital are closely related, but they are not the same. Understanding the distinction is essential for managing liquidity effectively. Cash flow tracks how money moves in and out of the business over time. Working capital reflects the difference between current assets and current liabilities, indicating whether the business can meet short-term obligations. A simple way to view the relationship is: Area Cash Flow Working Capital What It Measures Movement of cash Short-term liquidity position Focus Timing of inflows and outflows Available resources vs obligations Main Risk Cash gaps due to timing Capital tied up in assets A business can have positive working capital but still experience cash flow pressure if inflows are delayed. Similarly, strong cash flow can temporarily mask weak working capital if driven by financing or delayed payments. Also Read: Manage Business Cash Flow Effectively Where Capital Gets Trapped Inside The Cash Cycle Cash flow capital is often reduced not by one large issue, but by multiple smaller inefficiencies across the operating cycle. These areas are where liquidity tends to get trapped. 1. Receivables That Convert Too Slowly When customers take longer to pay, cash remains locked in outstanding invoices. This creates a gap between revenue recognition and actual cash availability. Atradius ’ 2025 UAE payment practices report found that overdue invoices affect 58% of B2B sales , showing how delayed receivables can reduce available cash flow capital even when revenue has already been recorded. 2. Inventory That Moves Slower Than Expected Inventory ties up cash until it is sold. Excess stock or slow-moving items increase the capital required to maintain operations. 3. Supplier Payments That Come Due Before Customer Cash Arrives When suppliers require early payment while customers pay later, the business must bridge the gap using its own cash or external capital. 4. Fixed Costs That Continue Regardless Of Revenue Timing Expenses such as salaries, rent, subscriptions, and logistics continue even when inflows are delayed. 5. Growth Spending Before Returns Are Realised Investments in hiring, marketing, or expansion often happen before revenue converts into cash, increasing short-term pressure. Why Revenue Growth Can Increase The Need For Cash Flow Capital Growth is often assumed to improve financial stability, but it can also increase pressure on cash flow capital. As a business grows, it typically: sells more but collects later holds more inventory hires more staff increases operating expenses This means cash outflows rise before inflows fully catch up. Without careful planning, growth can widen the gap between spending and cash availability. For example, a company may double its monthly sales, but if customers pay in 60 days and suppliers require faster payment, the business needs additional capital to sustain that growth. Also Read: Cash Flow Optimisation Strategies Techniques How To Know If A Business Needs More Cash Flow Capital Cash flow pressure does not always appear suddenly. In most cases, there are early indicators that capital available for operations is becoming insufficient. These signals are usually operational, not accounting-based. 1. Collections Are Slowing While Payments Remain Fixed If customer payments are delayed but supplier obligations continue on schedule, the business starts funding the gap internally. Over time, this reduces available liquidity. 2. Inventory Purchases Are Increasing Faster Than Sales Conversion When inventory builds up faster than it is sold, more cash gets tied up in stock. This reduces the capital available for other operating needs. 3. Short Term Borrowing Becomes Routine Occasional borrowing to manage timing gaps can be normal. However, when it becomes a recurring requirement, it indicates a structural cash flow capital issue. 4. Forecasted Cash Gaps Keep Reappearing If cash flow forecasts consistently show shortfalls, it suggests that the underlying operating cycle is not aligned with actual inflows and outflows. Also Read: Cash Flow Forecasting 5. Teams Delay Payments Or Spending Decisions When departments begin postponing payments or reducing necessary spend due to uncertainty, it often reflects underlying liquidity pressure. How Businesses Can Improve Cash Flow Capital Without Over Borrowing Increasing cash flow capital is not always about raising funds. In many cases, improving the efficiency of the operating cycle can release cash that is already within the business. 1. Shorten Collection Cycles Improving invoicing accuracy, follow-ups, and payment terms can reduce the time it takes for revenue to convert into cash. Even small improvements in collection timing can significantly improve liquidity. 2. Align Supplier Payments With Cash Inflows Negotiating better payment terms or aligning payment schedules with expected inflows helps reduce timing gaps. The goal is not to delay payments arbitrarily, but to match outflows more closely with inflows. 3. Reduce Cash Locked In Inventory Better demand planning and inventory management can prevent excess stock from tying up capital. Focusing on turnover rather than volume helps maintain balance. 4. Control Operating Spend Before It Becomes Fixed Small recurring costs and distributed team expenses often increase gradually. Without control, they raise the baseline cash requirement of the business. Related: Guide To Manage Overall Business Spending 5. Use Funding For Timing Gaps, Not Structural Issues External capital should support temporary mismatches between inflows and outflows. If funding is used to cover ongoing inefficiencies, it increases long-term risk. When External Capital Makes Sense While improving internal processes is essential, there are situations where external capital is appropriate. External funding can be useful when: the business has predictable demand but faces timing gaps between inflows and outflows growth opportunities require upfront investment before returns are realised supplier or inventory cycles require additional liquidity support However, relying on external capital without addressing underlying inefficiencies can create recurring pressure. The key is to distinguish between short-term liquidity needs and structural issues in the operating cycle. What Finance Teams Should Review Before Raising Or Allocating Capital Before deciding to raise or allocate additional capital, finance teams should evaluate how cash is currently moving through the business. A structured review helps identify whether the issue is timing, inefficiency, or genuine funding need. Review Area Why It Matters Receivables Ageing Shows how quickly invoices convert into cash Supplier Payment Terms Highlights outgoing cash commitments Inventory Turnover Identifies cash tied up in stock Monthly Fixed Costs Defines the minimum liquidity required Spend Commitments Captures obligations not yet reflected in cash balance Forecast Variance Indicates reliability of planning assumptions Also Read: Cash Management Control System UAE How Alaan Helps Finance Teams Protect Cash Flow Capital Cash flow capital is not only affected by receivables, inventory, or supplier terms. A significant portion of pressure comes from how operating spend is managed across the business. As companies grow, spending becomes more distributed across teams, vendors, and tools. Without structure, this leads to fragmented decisions, delayed visibility, and increasing baseline cash requirements. At Alaan , we help finance teams strengthen control over this execution layer so that cash outflows remain aligned with business priorities. Corporate Cards With Spend Controls And Vendor Restrictions Businesses can issue cards with defined limits and merchant controls, ensuring that spending stays within approved boundaries. Structured Approval Workflows Before Spend Happens All expenses can be routed through configurable approval flows, so decisions are reviewed before cash is committed. Real Time Visibility Into Operating Spend Finance teams can track spending across teams and categories as it happens, making it easier to identify unnecessary or unexpected outflows. Centralised Invoice And Receipt Capture All transactions are supported by linked documentation, improving accuracy and reducing gaps in financial records. Cleaner Reconciliation And Accounting Sync Integrations with systems like Xero, QuickBooks, NetSuite, and Microsoft Dynamics ensure that expense data flows directly into accounting. This ensures that cash flow capital is not gradually reduced by uncontrolled or untracked spending, and that finance teams can act before liquidity pressure becomes critical. Also Read: Understanding Spend Visibility Business Benefits Modern Expense Management Guide Track And Manage Business Expenses Conclusion Cash flow capital is not a formal accounting metric, but it reflects one of the most important realities of running a business: whether there is enough liquidity to support operations as cash moves through the system. Revenue, profit, and growth all matter, but they do not guarantee that cash will be available when needed. The timing of inflows and outflows, along with how efficiently capital is used, determines whether the business can operate smoothly. By improving collections, aligning supplier payments, managing inventory, and controlling operating spend, businesses can strengthen their cash flow capital without relying excessively on external funding. If you want to improve how your business tracks and controls cash outflows, you can explore how Alaan helps finance teams maintain visibility, enforce approvals, and keep spending aligned with financial priorities. Book a Demo Today! Frequently Asked Questions 1. Is Cash Flow Capital The Same As Working Capital No, working capital is a defined financial metric calculated as current assets minus current liabilities, while cash flow capital refers more broadly to the liquidity available to support cash movement in operations. 2. Can A Business Have High Revenue But Still Face Cash Flow Capital Issues Yes, if customer payments are delayed or costs are incurred before cash is received, revenue growth can increase pressure on available liquidity. 3. How Does Inventory Affect Cash Flow Capital Inventory ties up cash until it is sold. Slow-moving or excess inventory increases the amount of capital required to maintain operations. 4. When Should A Business Use External Capital To Support Cash Flow External capital is useful when there is a temporary timing gap between inflows and outflows, but it should not be used to cover ongoing inefficiencies. 5. What Is The Difference Between A Cash Flow Gap And A Working Capital Problem A cash flow gap is usually a short-term timing issue, while a working capital problem is more structural and related to how assets and liabilities are managed. 6. Which Financial Reports Help Track Cash Flow Capital Reports such as the cash flow statement, receivables ageing, payables schedules, and cash flow forecasts help provide a clearer view of liquidity and capital usage.

title: Your AI takes great notes. Does it do anything else?
summary: Meeting intelligence is only valuable if something happens after the meeting ends.
body_text: In this blog 01 Great meetings shouldn't end with a summary nobody acts on - Jumplink to Great meetings shouldn't end with a summary nobody acts on 02 Here's what work looks like when AI actually follows through - Jumplink to Here's what work looks like when AI actually follows through 03 One AI layer to govern beats six you didn't ask for - Jumplink to One AI layer to govern beats six you didn't ask for 04 Zoom Workplace is already built this way - Jumplink to Zoom Workplace is already built this way Share this post Robin Bunevich Product Marketing Manager, Zoom AI Robin Bunevich is a Product Marketing Manager at Zoom. She oversees product marketing and strategy for Zoom AI. After three years of leading marketing for Zoom’s Event Solution products, and launching one of the fastest growing products at Zoom, Zoom Events, she is now focused on helping organizations seamlessly adopt AI into their workflows. Prior to Zoom, she ran marketing for live events at The New York Times, and was instrumental in helping the organization transition to a fully virtual events program in March of 2020. At Zoom, Robin uses her 15 plus years of marketing and advertising experience to drive awareness and adoption for Zoom’s AI solutions. Every day, knowledge workers generate more useful information than any organization can act on. Decisions get made in meetings. Context surfaces in conversations. Answers emerge in discussions that nobody outside the room ever hears. Getting all of that down somewhere has largely been solved. AI note-taking is just the beginning. The harder problem is what happens next. Many organizations have gotten very good at recording knowledge, but rarely make it count. The summary exists. The action item is documented. And somewhere between the meeting ending and the work beginning, there's an email or a ping or — surprise — another meeting! And the work meant to get done doesn't get done at all. Want to see what this looks like in practice? Here's the full picture Great meetings shouldn't end with a summary nobody acts on Consider what a single productive meeting produces: decisions that need to be communicated, tasks that need owners, questions that need answers, follow-ups that need to happen before the next conversation. A good AI note-taker captures all of it faithfully. Then a human reads the summary, figures out what matters, creates tasks in a separate system, and manually bridges the gap to the next step. The AI note-taker captured the conversation. A human still has to do all the work of turning it into action. Here's what work looks like when AI actually follows through When capture, context, and action are connected, work can move differently. With the right setup, a meeting ends and summaries can be automatically routed to the right people with owners and deadlines attached. A question that came up mid-meeting can be answered by searching across past conversations, shared documents, and connected systems. The follow-up promised to a customer can be drafted with the conversation context already woven in. And none of this means that everyone has to be on the same platform. Many AI note-takers work wherever meetings happen — video calls, phone calls, in-person conversations — because they use system audio rather than being built for one specific tool. Many AI note-takers are designed to follow your teams across meeting environments, not just a single platform. One AI layer to govern beats six you didn't ask for Many organizations have already accumulated multiple AI tools, each with its own data policies, compliance requirements, and management dashboard. Research shows employees using AI-enabled collaboration features reclaim an average of three hours per week, but that value is hard to measure and harder to govern when it's spread across tools IT doesn't control.* When capture, context, and action run through a single platform, IT gets a unified place to set policies, one control panel, and one way to manage it all. The intelligence is built to scale. The overhead doesn't have to. Zoom Workplace is already built this way This isn't a vision of what AI could do someday. It's what happens when capture, context, and action run through one platform. My Notes works across Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, in-person — using system audio. AI features built into Zoom Workplace are designed to add intelligence across meetings, chat, and phone, helping keep context connected. And ZoomMate can connect that intelligence to the tools your teams already use, helping turn conversations into completed tasks, drafted follow-ups, and finished work. My Notes and core AI features are included with eligible paid Zoom Workplace plans. ZoomMate is available as a paid add-on that brings AI agents, workflows, and the ability to connect to supported apps like Salesforce, Jira, Google Drive, and OneDrive. Work can move from conversation to completion. One platform, a unified way to manage it, no matter where your team does their best work. Ready to see what an AI system looks like in practice? Explore Zoom Workplace *Deloitte, commissioned by Zoom, "The Productivity Payoff of Next Generation Collaboration," 2025.

Earnings webcast Audio Earnings snapshot PDF Achieves second quarter revenue growth of 10% as reported and 9% organic, and CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growth of 11% as reported and 10% organic. Strong volume-driven CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growth including benefits from IDEXX's innovations and expansion of diagnostics utilization. IDEXX inVue Dx™ installed base surpasses 9,000 instruments, supported by over 1,600 placements during the quarter. WESTBROOK, Maine--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- IDEXX Laboratories, Inc. (NASDAQ: IDXX) , a global leader in pet healthcare innovation, today announced second quarter results. Second Quarter Results The Company reports revenues of $1,217 million for the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 10% as reported and 9% organic, driven by Companion Animal Group ("CAG") growth of 9% as reported and organic, Water revenue growth of 15% as reported and 13% organic, and LPD revenue growth of 11% as reported and 9% organic. Second quarter earnings per diluted share (“EPS”) were $4.27, an increase of 18% as reported and 15% on a comparable basis. Second quarter EPS included $0.14 per share in tax benefits from share-based compensation and $0.06 per share benefit from year-over-year currency changes. “Our second quarter results reflect the strength of our Technology for Life strategy, with continued innovation across our Catalyst, Fecal Dx, and IDEXX inVue Dx platforms supporting deeper customer adoption and higher diagnostic utilization,” said Mike Erickson, President and Chief Executive Officer. “This is the kind of durable, compounding growth we're building for the long term, helping veterinarians see more and do more for their patients while creating lasting value for our shareholders.” Second Quarter Performance Highlights Companion Animal Group (“CAG”) CAG revenue growth was led by CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growth of 11% as reported and 10% organic, including 14% reported and 12% organic gains in International regions, and 10% reported and organic growth in the U.S., outpacing sector growth levels. Additional U.S. companion animal practice key metrics are available in the Q2 2026 Earnings Snapshot accessible on the IDEXX website, www.idexx.com/investors . Exceptional commercial execution - including strong volume gains, net customer expansion, benefits from IDEXX innovation, and growth of the premium instrument installed base - drove double-digit CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growth. IDEXX VetLab™ consumables generated 15% reported and 14% organic revenue growth, supported by testing utilization gains, including benefits from recent product launches and net new customer growth with 11% expansion of the IDEXX global premium instrument installed base and net price gains. Reference laboratory diagnostic and consulting services generated 11% reported and 10% organic revenue growth, driven by higher testing volumes and net new customer gains. Rapid assay products revenues increased 1% as reported and on an organic basis, driven by net price benefits and an easing of the volume impacts from adoption of the Catalyst™ Pancreatic Lipase Test, which has shifted some testing across modalities. CAG Diagnostics capital instrument revenues decreased 19% as reported and 20% on an organic basis, lapping the Q2 2025 broad availability of IDEXX inVue Dx, with current-year period revenue benefiting from over 1,600 IDEXX inVue Dx placements. Veterinary software, services and diagnostic imaging systems revenues grew 12% on a reported and organic basis for the quarter, with benefits from cloud-native software growth and installed base expansion. Diagnostic imaging systems delivered another record quarter of installations, led by ImageVue™ DR50 Plus. Water Water revenues grew 15% as reported and 13% organic for the quarter, reflecting solid organic growth in the U.S. and Europe. Livestock, Poultry and Dairy (“LPD”) LPD revenues increased 11% as reported and 9% organic for the quarter, led by strong growth in the Americas. Gross Profit and Operating Profit Gross profit increased 12% as reported and 11% on a comparable basis. Gross margin of 64.0% increased 140 basis points as reported and 120 basis points on a comparable basis, supported by strong recurring revenue volume gains, operational productivity initiatives, and net price realization. Operating margin was 35.0% for the quarter, higher than the prior year period by 140 basis points as reported and by 110 basis points on a comparable basis. Operating margin results reflect a 10% operating expense increase as reported and 9% growth on a comparable basis. Operating expense growth supported expansion of commercial capabilities, advancement of the Company's innovation agenda, and enabling information technology investments. 2026 Growth and Financial Performance Outlook The Company is updating its full year revenue growth guidance range to $4,700 million - $4,745 million, or reported growth of 9.1% - 10.3%, an increase of $5 million at midpoint, net of a $15 million reduction to projected revenues from a stronger U.S. dollar. The Company is increasing its outlook for organic revenue growth to 8.5% - 9.7%, an increase of 0.4% at midpoint, reflecting operational performance. The Company increased its full year reported operating margin outlook to 32.3% - 32.5%, bringing the projected full year operating profit margin expansion to 70 - 90 basis points as reported and on a comparable basis. This outlook benefits from strong second quarter operating performance, while advancing strategic investment priorities. The Company updated its EPS outlook range to $14.69 - $14.94, reflecting increased reported growth of 12% - 14% and 13% - 15% comparable growth. At midpoint this reflects benefits of $0.14 per share from operational performance; $0.05 from higher share-based compensation benefits and a $0.05 headwind from updated estimates for foreign exchange impacts. About IDEXX Laboratories, Inc. IDEXX is a global leader in pet healthcare innovation. Our diagnostic and software products and services create clarity in the complex, constantly evolving world of veterinary medicine. We support longer, fuller lives for pets by delivering insights and solutions that help the veterinary community around the world make confident decisions—to advance medical care, improve efficiency, and build thriving practices. Our innovations also help measure the safety of milk and water across the world and maintain the health and well-being of people and livestock. Statement Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Measures The following defines terms and conventions and provides reconciliations regarding certain measures used in this earnings release and/or the accompanying earnings conference call that are not required by, or presented in accordance with, generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America ("GAAP"), otherwise referred to as non-GAAP financial measures. To supplement the Company’s consolidated results presented in accordance with GAAP, the Company has disclosed non-GAAP financial measures that exclude or adjust certain items. Management believes these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful supplemental information for its and investors’ evaluation of the Company’s business performance and liquidity and are useful for period-over-period comparisons of the performance of the Company’s business and its liquidity and to the performance and liquidity of our peers. While management believes that these non-GAAP financial measures are useful in evaluating the Company’s business, this information should be considered as supplemental in nature and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the related financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. In addition, these non-GAAP financial measures may not be the same as similarly titled measures reported by other companies. Constant currency - Constant currency references are non-GAAP financial measures which exclude the impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates and are consistent with how management evaluates our performance and comparisons with prior and future periods. We estimate the net impacts of currency on our revenue, gross profit, operating profit, and EPS results by restating results to the average exchange rates or exchange rate assumptions for the comparative period, which includes adjusting for the estimated impacts of foreign currency hedging transactions and certain impacts on our effective tax rates. These estimated currency changes impacted second quarter 2026 results as follows: increased gross profit growth by 1.1%, increased gross margin expansion 20 basis points, increased operating expense growth by 0.5%, increased operating profit growth by 1.6%, increased operating profit margin growth by 30 basis points, and increased EPS growth by 1.7%. Constant currency revenue growth represents the percentage change in revenue during the applicable period, as compared to the prior year period, excluding the impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates. See the supplementary analysis of results below for revenue percentage change from currency for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and refer to the 2026 Growth and Financial Performance Outlook section of this earnings release for estimated foreign currency exchange rate impacts on 2026 projections and estimates. Growth and organic revenue growth - All references to growth and organic growth refer to growth compared to the equivalent prior year period unless specifically noted. Organic revenue growth is a non-GAAP financial measure that represents the percentage change in revenue, as compared to the same period for the prior year, net of the effect of changes in foreign currency exchange rates, certain business acquisitions, and divestitures. Management believes that reporting organic revenue growth provides useful information to investors by facilitating easier comparisons of our revenue performance with prior and future periods and to the performance of our peers. Organic revenue growth should be considered in addition to, and not as a replacement of or a superior measure to, revenue growth reported in accordance with GAAP. See the supplementary analysis of results below for a reconciliation of reported revenue growth to organic revenue growth for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026. Please refer to the constant currency note above for a summary of foreign currency exchange rate impacts. Please refer to the 2026 Growth and Financial Performance Outlook section of this earnings release for estimated full year 2026 organic revenue growth for the Company and CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growth. The percentage change in revenue resulting from acquisitions represents revenues during the current year period, limited to the initial 12 months from the date of the acquisition, that are directly attributable to business acquisitions. Revenue from acquisitions is expected to have an immaterial impact on projected full year 2026 revenue growth and no impact on CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growth. We exclude from organic revenue growth the effect of changes in foreign currency exchange rates because changes in foreign currency exchange rates are not under management’s control, are subject to volatility, and can obscure underlying business trends. We calculate the impact on revenue resulting from changes in foreign currency exchange rates by applying the difference between the weighted average exchange rates during the current year period and the comparable prior year period to foreign currency denominated revenues for the prior year period. We also exclude from organic revenue growth the effect of certain business acquisitions and divestitures because the nature, size, and number of these transactions can vary dramatically from period to period, and because they either require or generate cash as an inherent consequence of the transaction, and therefore can also obscure underlying business and operating trends. We consider acquisitions to be a business when all three elements of inputs, processes, and outputs are present, consistent with ASU 2017-01, “ Business Combinations: (Topic 805) Clarifying the Definition of a Business .” We do not consider acquired assets to be a business if substantially all the fair value of the assets acquired is concentrated in a single identifiable asset or group of similar identifiable assets. A typical acquisition that we do not consider a business is a customer relationship asset acquisition, which does not have all elements necessary to operate a business, such as employees or infrastructure. Revenue from these customers acquired is included in organic revenue growth because we believe the efforts required to convert and retain these acquired customers are similar in nature to our efforts to obtain and retain our existing customer base. Free cash flow conversion, or the net income to free cash flow ratio, is a non-GAAP financial measure that is defined as free cash flow, with respect to a measurement period, divided by net income for the same period. To calculate trailing twelve-month net income to free cash flow ratio for the twelve months ended June 30, 2026, we have deducted purchases of property and equipment of approximately $117 million from net cash provided from operating activities of approximately $1,372 million, divided by net income of approximately $1,140 million. Debt to Adjusted EBITDA (Leverage Ratios ) - Adjusted EBITDA, gross debt, and net debt are non-GAAP financial measures. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, non-recurring transaction expenses incurred in connection with acquisitions, share-based compensation expense, and certain other non-cash losses and charges. Management believes that reporting Adjusted EBITDA, gross debt, and net debt in the Debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratios provides supplemental analysis to help investors further evaluate the Company's business performance and available borrowing capacity under the Company's credit facility. Adjusted EBITDA, gross debt, and net debt should be considered in addition to, and not as replacements of or superior measures to, net income or total debt reported in accordance with GAAP.
